item.title: Why Africa is without vaccine for latest Ebola strain — Africa CDC
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr Jean Kaseya, has blamed a lack of international interest for the absence of an approved vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, saying the situation might have been different if the outbreak were affecting Western countries. Kaseya made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where he called for greater African investment in vaccine research and manufacturing. He said, “I can tell you, if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccine will already be available. Why this vaccine today is not available? Because some of our partners decided to consider this issue as an African issue, they were not interested.” The Africa CDC chief, however, said the agency was taking steps to address the gap, including supporting clinical trials of vaccine candidates. He disclosed that an African manufacturer in Egypt was conducting clinical trials of a potential vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain. Kaseya also said the agency was working with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to explore clinical trials and compassionate use of Ervebo, a vaccine developed for the Zaire strain of Ebola. He stressed that the continent had the expertise and capacity to advance vaccine development, adding that Africa should not continue to depend solely on external partners during public health emergencies. “We don’t want to see Africa left behind. We have the knowledge, we have people with intelligence, we have capacity to manufacture vaccines, and we need to move on,” he said. Kaseya also called for greater domestic funding and improved coordination among African countries and international partners. He said 28 African countries had contributed funding to support the response to the current outbreak. The Bundibugyo strain has no licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment. The outbreak, declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in May 2026, has caused more than 9,000 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths, according to Congolese health authorities The disease has also been detected in other countries, with the Kenyan Health Ministry reporting a ninth case in the country on Tuesday, prompting concerns over cross-border transmission. Nigeria also confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20. The patient, a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda, is receiving medical care, while health authorities have identified 44 contacts for monitoring. The post Why Africa is without vaccine for latest Ebola strain — Africa CDC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Mass Effect Is Not Dead Yet as the Amazon Series Is Still Going Forward
item.description: Oct. 21 was a rough day for Mass Effect fans, as EA announced that it would be closing its development studio BioWare and canceling the fifth installment in the series. At least, the franchise isn't vanishing entirely. Amazon MGM has not pulled the plug on the upcoming Mass Effect TV series, which will move forward.

item.title: Liverpool release Diogo Jota biography 'Forever in our Hearts' with profits funding grassroots programme
item.description: Liverpool release Diogo Jota biography 'Forever in our Hearts' with profits funding grassroots programme Liverpool have released Forever in our Hearts , a new biography celebrating the life and legacy of Diogo Jota , with all of the club's profits funding a grassroots football programme to be established in his name. Every purchase supports the LFC Foundation, according to the club . The book, published by Reach Sport, is available now from official LFC stores and online. It has been written by Portuguese author and former professional footballer José Delgado, and traces Jota's journey from his early years in Portugal to becoming a Premier League star and firm Anfield favourite. Delgado drew on extensive interviews with family members, friends, teammates and coaches. Contributors include Jota's wife Rute, his parents Isabel and Joaquim, former Liverpool manager Jürgen Klopp and more than 90 others who knew him best. "This book began as an opportunity to help preserve Diogo's memory at a moment of profound sadness. My commitment throughout was to tell his story with care, honesty and respect for Diogo, André, and the family and friends who loved them." - José Delgado The biography follows Jota through a period that culminated in Premier League success with Liverpool and UEFA Nations League glory with Portugal. It also celebrates the bond he shared with his brother André, and reflects on the tragic events that followed his marriage to childhood sweetheart Rute, and the outpouring of grief from across the football world after the deaths of Diogo and André in July 2025. Delgado said the willingness of those closest to the brothers to share their memories shaped the project. "What moved me most was the generosity of those closest to them. Family members, teammates, coaches and friends shared their memories to help future generations understand the person Diogo was, and their love for both brothers can be felt on every page," he said. "The unique bond between Diogo and Liverpool FC" The author added that his research left him struck by how strongly Jota was connected to the club. "While researching the book, I came to understand the unique bond between Diogo and Liverpool FC. Everywhere I went, people spoke not only of his talent, but also his humility, commitment and character." - José Delgado "My hope is that Forever in our Hearts serves as a fitting tribute to Diogo's life and legacy, and ensures his story continues to inspire others for years to come," Delgado said. The release is the latest way Liverpool have honoured their eternal No.20. Earlier this year, a permanent memorial to Diogo and André Silva was unveiled outside Anfield, giving supporters a space to reflect on the brothers' lives and their lasting impact on the football community.

item.title: Rob Gronkowski names whether he’d prefer to play with Drake Maye or Caleb Williams
item.description: Photo by John Nacion/Getty Images Thursday Night Football will see Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears host Drake Maye and his New England Patriots in what will be one of the matchups of Week Seven. Following a rocky start to the season, Maye finally looks to have found his rhythm again for the Patriots. Having thrown one touchdown in the opening three games, the 24-year-old has turned things around with 10 touchdowns in his last three games. Chicago received a massive boost at the weekend after they welcomed Williams back to their starting line-up. The quarterback looked like he had never been away after throwing for over 300 yards against the Atlanta Falcons. This is set to be a real battle between two brilliant quarterbacks but Rob Gronkowski already knows which one he would have preferred to play with. Rob Gronkowski chooses between Drake Maye and Caleb Williams The start to the year for Maye was a huge shock after what was such an impressive 2025 season. Fortunately for the Patriots, Maye has been able to turn things around as Gronkowski shared just why he would love to play with the 24-year-old QB. “They’re both in the right situations. They really are, and Ben Johnson, I feel like, hit a home run where he landed with the head coaching situation with Caleb there. It’s so hard because, with the systems, you got to have that quarterback for the system that you’re presenting to the table as an offensive coordinator and as an organisation,” Gronkowski said on the Up & Adams Show. “I feel like they both landed in the right places. There’s no doubt about that, but if I had to choose a quarterback, this is tough. This is tough, it really is, but I’m going to go with Drake Maye. I really am, Kay. I just like the touch on his ball. “I feel like, in the end, Drake Maye would be, for me as well as a player, the ideal quarterback. I mean, I’m not saying I wouldn’t have chemistry with Caleb, but I feel like Drake Maye and I would be able to be on the same page with the chemistry going into games. Just the way that he can process defences, I feel like he’s going to get better and better and better.” Thursday’s game at Soldier Field has the potential to be one for the ages with both teams heading into it in fine form. Gronkowski’s comments could now even give Williams some extra motivation going into the game. Of course, Gronk has loyalties to the Patriots following his time in New England but he has shown his belief in Maye despite his early season struggles. Williams is only going into his fourth game of the season on Thursday as he looks to throw for more than two touchdowns for the first time this year. item.title: Shaun Maloney makes unexpected admission after stunning Hearts victory
item.description: Shaun Maloney makes unexpected admission after stunning Hearts victory Celtic assistant manager Shaun Maloney has played down the significance of Sunday’s emphatic 7-1 victory over Hearts, insisting the result was simply another step in the team’s recent progress. Martin O’Neill’s side produced a sensational attacking display against last season’s title challengers. However, despite the magnitude of the result, Maloney believes Celtic’s performance was a continuation of the improvements shown in recent weeks rather than a defining moment in their season. Speaking ahead of Thursday’s Europa League clash with Celta Vigo, he said: “You’d probably have to ask the players in terms of their view. From a coaching staff, probably not. “I think the Motherwell game coming straight back, I think everyone got back a couple of days before that game to produce that performance, because Motherwell make it quite tough in trying to control the ball. “No, it didn’t feel that seismic, Hearts. I know it was a really good performance. Some of the attacking stuff was really good. It doesn’t feel like that big moment. I feel like it’s just a continuation of that week. “We’ve got a fair bit to work on and continue to work on. So it didn’t feel like that for me. Maybe the guys or the players might have felt differently, but for us it was good. “Everyone was committed with and without the ball. So that was probably what we took from it as a staff or the coaches anyway.” HAVE YOUR SAY – Join the Celtic conversation in our comments section below… Celtic in the Fifties by Matt Corr, in two volumes, both published on 4th September 2026 by Celtic Star Books. item.title: Dolphins news: Speeding up team development, injury updates, Jets game prep
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Caleb Douglas #7 of the Miami Dolphins gets set during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are the youngest team in the NFL this season, kick-starting their franchise rebuild with an influx of rookies and second-year players. The team hopes to move from a consistently mediocre franchise that fights just to make a cameo in the playoffs to one that consistently battles for deep postseason runs. While the goal is lofty, the Dolphins have had to tear down their roster for 2026, taking a massive immediate salary cap hit to get the future cap under control. Development is the Dolphins’ name for the game, as they hope their young roster can learn and grow quickly. South Florida Sun Sentinel columnist Chris Perkins took a look at how Miami is hoping to speed along that learning curve with a weekly addition to the practice schedule: Every Thursday, after the Miami Dolphins conclude their regular practice, many of the second- and third-team players gather for a brief 7-on-7 session. It sounds minimal, but coaches and players say the extra work is helpful because it better acquaints backups on Miami’s offense and defense, offers more hands-on coaching, and familiarizes them with playing alongside the starters… “It’s been really important to me,” said [head coach Jeff] Hafley, who detests 7-on-7 sessions during training camp. “I think regardless of where you’re at, I think we’re still in a developmental league.” The 7 on 7s are only seven or eight plays, but the repetitions and additional coaching add up over the course of a season for Dolphins backup players, most of whom spend midweek practices playing on the scout team. And here’s the big thing: in the 7-on-7 sessions, backups run the Dolphins offense and defense, they’d run if they’re suddenly inserted into a game. When they play on the scout team during midweek practices, they run the opponent’s offense and defense. Welcome to the Splash Zone, a collection of Dolphins stories from around the web curated for you each morning. item.title: Women's Tour de France 2027 to feature stage through central London
item.description: FILE PHOTO - A general view of the Tour de France logo on a flag. Due to coronavirus restrictions, the Tour de France will not be able go ahead on 27 June as originally planned, organizers said. (is associated with: «Women's Tour de France 2027 to feature stage through central London») David Davies/PA Wire/dpa Next summer's Tour de France Femmes will include what promises to be a spectacular 18 kilometre team time trial through the heart of London, finishing on the Mall. The third stage of the women's race on August 2 will take riders past the Houses of Parliament, Tower of London and St Paul's Cathedral, crossing Tower Bridge and going through both Trafalgar Square and Hyde Park before finishing in front of Buckingham Palace. Details of the stage were part of Thursday's full route reveal for the men's and women's Tours, as Britain becomes the first country outside France to host the start of both races in the same year, with stages passing through Scotland, England and Wales. The other UK routes were announced earlier this year as Britain prepares to welcome the men's Tour for a fifth time and the women's race for the first time. The women's Tour will start on July 30 with an 87km stage between Leeds and Manchester and a day later there will be echoes of 2014 with a 154km stage from Manchester to Sheffield, taking in several of the climbs used by the men's Tour 13 years earlier. After London the Tour heads across the channel and towards a showdown in the Massif Central, with a summit finish to stage seven on La Loge des Gardes, more than 3,000 metres of climbing on stage eight to Clermont-Ferrand and a final fight for yellow on the Puy de Dome on stage nine. The men's race will start on July 2 with a 184km largely flat stage from Edinburgh to Carlisle. A 223km stage two will take the peloton from Keswick to Liverpool via the Forest of Bowland and a challenging 223km stage three goes through the heart of Wales between Welshpool and Cardiff. After crossing into France, the Tour will make its way from Normandy to the Alps via the Jura mountains and then across the Massif Central towards a final showdown in the Pyrenees, where the battle for yellow should be settled. Six mountain stages will include three summit finishes on the Grand Colombier, Les Saisies and the Col du Portet. Key to the overall battle will be a total of 71 kilometres of time trialling on stages seven and 16. The final stage on to the Champs-Elysees in Paris will once again include three ascents of the climb to Montmartre which has become so popular since the 2024 Olympics, reshaping the traditional sprint finish to the Tour as Mathieu van der Poel took a thrilling victory this summer. Tadej Pogacar can target a record-breaking sixth Tour title next summer after joining Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain on five this summer, although the Slovenian missed Thursday's route announcement as he continues his recovery from a crash at the Vuelta a Espana.
item.content:encoded: FILE PHOTO - A general view of the Tour de France logo on a flag. Due to coronavirus restrictions, the Tour de France will not be able go ahead on 27 June as originally planned, organizers said. (is associated with: «Women's Tour de France 2027 to feature stage through central London») David Davies/PA Wire/dpa Next summer's Tour de France Femmes will include what promises to be a spectacular 18 kilometre team time trial through the heart of London, finishing on the Mall. The third stage of the women's race on August 2 will take riders past the Houses of Parliament, Tower of London and St Paul's Cathedral, crossing Tower Bridge and going through both Trafalgar Square and Hyde Park before finishing in front of Buckingham Palace. Details of the stage were part of Thursday's full route reveal for the men's and women's Tours, as Britain becomes the first country outside France to host the start of both races in the same year, with stages passing through Scotland, England and Wales. The other UK routes were announced earlier this year as Britain prepares to welcome the men's Tour for a fifth time and the women's race for the first time. The women's Tour will start on July 30 with an 87km stage between Leeds and Manchester and a day later there will be echoes of 2014 with a 154km stage from Manchester to Sheffield, taking in several of the climbs used by the men's Tour 13 years earlier. After London the Tour heads across the channel and towards a showdown in the Massif Central, with a summit finish to stage seven on La Loge des Gardes, more than 3,000 metres of climbing on stage eight to Clermont-Ferrand and a final fight for yellow on the Puy de Dome on stage nine. The men's race will start on July 2 with a 184km largely flat stage from Edinburgh to Carlisle. A 223km stage two will take the peloton from Keswick to Liverpool via the Forest of Bowland and a challenging 223km stage three goes through the heart of Wales between Welshpool and Cardiff. After crossing into France, the Tour will make its way from Normandy to the Alps via the Jura mountains and then across the Massif Central towards a final showdown in the Pyrenees, where the battle for yellow should be settled. Six mountain stages will include three summit finishes on the Grand Colombier, Les Saisies and the Col du Portet. Key to the overall battle will be a total of 71 kilometres of time trialling on stages seven and 16. The final stage on to the Champs-Elysees in Paris will once again include three ascents of the climb to Montmartre which has become so popular since the 2024 Olympics, reshaping the traditional sprint finish to the Tour as Mathieu van der Poel took a thrilling victory this summer. Tadej Pogacar can target a record-breaking sixth Tour title next summer after joining Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain on five this summer, although the Slovenian missed Thursday's route announcement as he continues his recovery from a crash at the Vuelta a Espana.

item.title: Bayern Munich sell shares to Viessmann in deal estimated at €250m
item.description: FILE PHOTO - The FC Bayern Munich logo can be seen at the club's premises on Saebener Strasse. (is associated with: «Bayern Munich sell shares to Viessmann in deal estimated at €250m») Sven Hoppe/dpa Bayern Munich are selling shares from the professional football division to long-time partners Viessmann Generations Group for an estimated €250 million ($281 million). Bayern said on Wednesday that Viessmann will acquire 5% of the shares which at the end the transaction will rise to close to 6.7% via an increase in capital. No financial figures were given beyond that. Bayern regulations stipulate that the parent club must hold 70% of the shares and the remaining 30% can be split among four shareholders. The Viessmann equity package is the fourth and final one, with sports goods makers Adidas, insurers Allianz and car makers Audi the other three. "This step strengthens the ownership structure of FC Bayern München AG. A further substantial strengthening of our equity base also gives us greater flexibility in a time of constant change," Bayern president Herbert Hainer said. Viessmann have been a Bayern partner since 2018. The family-owned company operating in more than 40 countries specializes in heating technology products and power grid infrastructure. The news also means that chairman Max Viessmann is to join Bayern's supervisory board as a 10th member. "FC Bayern is one of Europe's most successful clubs, with clear values and a strong sense of social responsibility," he said. "We want to play our part in maintaining a strong FC Bayern."

Here you can watch it again in all its perfection. In 80 out of 100 attempts, that ball probably ends up in the upper tier of the Estadio Santiago Bernabéu. Last night, though, it absolutely flew in. item.title: Are fresh US-Israeli strikes on Iran in the pipeline?
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, October 22: The New York Times's sources report plans for fresh strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections. In other news, the French Senate publishes a 30-step proposal for how to "take back control", just days after protests gave way to riots. Also, how software engineers found and patched up bugs in the language that makes up 70 percent of the internet. Finally, the story of a man for whom what happened in Vegas did not stay there.

item.title: Perez wants to race at Le Mans with Verstappen and Alonso: ‘That would be great’
item.description: Sergio Perez would love to compete in the 24 Hours of Le Mans alongside Max Verstappen and Fernando Alonso , the Cadillac driver confirms in an exclusive interview with GPblog. The Mexican sees the prospect of having fun with both drivers as a key reason for wanting to line up alongside them. GPblog asked Perez whether he would be interested in competing in the 24 Hours of Le Mans with the two world champions, with the 36-year-old responding positively to the idea. Perez explained he would be keen to compete together, while acknowledging that the schedules of all three F1 drivers would have to align."Yeah, that would be something great to do. You know, with them. But I think that with them it's also hard to make sure that it happens at the right time, at the right moment," he said. Aside from the fact that Perez would have two of the strongest possible teammates in Verstappen and Alonso for a potential entry in the prestigious endurance race, having an enjoyable experience is just as important to him. "Certainly, I would like to do Le Mans with drivers I know I can have fun with. And they are certainly two drivers I can have a lot of fun with," Perez continued, with a smile appearing on his face at the thought. Perez has spoken about competing at Le Mans before Perez has previously expressed interest in competing in the French 24-hour race. In 2024, he said that the 24 Hours of Le Mans was the only race outside Formula 1 that really appealed to him. At the time, he did not name any drivers he would like to take on the challenge with, but he would certainly be keen to compete alongside Verstappen and Alonso. Verstappen and Alonso have repeatedly said in recent years that they would like to compete together in the 24 Hours of Le Mans. In 2023, Verstappen revealed that he had discussed it with the Aston Martin driver. According to the Dutchman, Alonso had said he would only return if he could race alongside Verstappen. In February 2025, Verstappen again spoke about competing together. At the time, he named his father, Jos, as a possible third driver, although he said Jos was not interested. Sebastian Vettel was later mentioned as another potential teammate. Verstappen also made it clear that he would only compete at Le Mans if he had a car capable of fighting for victory. He said: "I don’t think it’s going to happen next year, but maybe in the future.” Verstappen himself confirmed that Le Mans is not currently on his schedule for 2027.

item.title: Jaden McDaniels admits he never even wanted to join the Timberwolves after $40m extension
item.description: Photo by Tyler Clouse/Getty Images Jaden McDaniels has become one of the best perimeter defenders in the NBA and is a key player for the Minnesota Timberwolves. The 26-year-old has been a part of the team since he was drafted in 2020. He is entering his seventh season now and has committed his future to the Wolves. According to ESPN, McDaniels has put pen to paper on a rare one-year extension worth $40 million that will keep him in Minnesota through the 2029-30 season. But if he had got his wish six years ago, he would be as far away from the Timberwolves as possible. Jaden McDaniels says he never wanted to join the Minnesota Timberwolves McDaniels was selected 28th in the 2020 draft by the Los Angeles Lakers before his draft rights eventually ended up with the Minnesota Timberwolves. Of course, getting into a team is a dream for any youngster, but the defender was praying that the Wolves would stay away from him. He just didn’t want to go there. However, as fate would have it, McDaniels had to join the Minnesota side, but luckily for him, that has changed his life over the last six years. Now, after signing a lucrative extension, he has admitted why he didn’t want to join the Timberwolves all those years ago. “In the draft process, I didn’t know where I was going. This was actually the team I was trying to stay away from,” he told Dane Moore on X : “So I ended up coming here not knowing how it was gonna be. The first year was terrible, but after that, we started winning, building, getting better and adding more pieces. It has just been a good situation.” When asked why he was against a move to the Wolves, he said: “Yeah, they were just bad. Just bad as f***.” The Timberwolves were coming off a 19–45 campaign and stuck near the bottom of the Western Conference before the 2020 draft, so McDaniels’ stance is understandable. But together, the player and the team have grown immensely over the last few years and are now seen as one of the contenders in the Western Conference. item.title: Joe Burrow Reacts to JD Vance Visiting Bengals Practice
item.description: Vice President JD Vance, a lifelong Cincinnati Bengals fan, returned to his home region in Ohio on Wednesday for several local events. He began his Wednesday schedule at the FBI field office in Sycamore Township. Later, Vance traveled to the Sharonville Convention Center to speak at a campaign rally, where supporters carried “restoring common sense” signs. Afterward, a six-SUV motorcade took Vance to the practice fields outside Paycor Stadium, where he visited the locker room, met head coach Zac Taylor, and even got a football. Oct 11, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) walks off the field after the game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Joe Burrow Reacts to Vice President JD Vance Dropping By Bengals Practice Even with Vance touring the facility, star quarterback Joe Burrow said he didn’t get to meet him. Team owner Mike Brown broke the news that Vance was on the sideline, and Burrow kept his response simple when reporters asked about it. “We did not,” Burrow said. “He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn’t get to.” Talking about Vance’s visit and what he feels about it, Burrow said, “A lot of people around. That’s what I love about what I do is it brings a lot of people together. And people want to take time out of their day to come and watch what we do, and watch what I do, and watch all the work that I put in to come and watch greatness. Everybody in the locker room, that’s why we do what we do. And whether it’s on the TV, whether it’s in person, whether it’s on the practice field, that’s what we do.” Joe Burrow said Bengals owner Mike Brown told him at the start of practice JD Vance would be attending Burrow on the vice presidential visit to Paycor Stadium: pic.twitter.com/hAktahQopW — Charlie Clifford (@char_cliff) October 21, 2026 Vance, who is from Middletown and owns a home in Cincinnati, once watched the Bengals lose a 2006 playoff game while deployed in Iraq. Now, coming to Burrow, the Bengals QB is dealing with some injuries. In Week 5, when they beat the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium, he jammed his left thumb trying to grab a loose ball. The medical staff checked him out on the sidelines, wrapped his hand up, and Burrow went right back into the game. Before that, in a close 30-27 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3, he got sacked at the 46-yard line with 53 seconds left. But even after losing to the Jacksonville Jaguars the next week, Burrow didn’t panic about the team’s future and kept things in perspective, saying , “We had our opportunities the last two weeks, but certainly this isn’t Armageddon or anything. We’re still in a great spot and feel really good about our team”. Coming off their Week 6 bye, the Bengals resumed practice to regain their footing after losing two of their previous three games. Oct 11, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) walks off the field after the game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Joe Burrow Reacts to Vice President JD Vance Dropping By Bengals Practice Even with Vance touring the facility, star quarterback Joe Burrow said he didn’t get to meet him. Team owner Mike Brown broke the news that Vance was on the sideline, and Burrow kept his response simple when reporters asked about it. “We did not,” Burrow said. “He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn’t get to.” Talking about Vance’s visit and what he feels about it, Burrow said, “A lot of people around. That’s what I love about what I do is it brings a lot of people together. And people want to take time out of their day to come and watch what we do, and watch what I do, and watch all the work that I put in to come and watch greatness. Everybody in the locker room, that’s why we do what we do. And whether it’s on the TV, whether it’s in person, whether it’s on the practice field, that’s what we do.” Joe Burrow said Bengals owner Mike Brown told him at the start of practice JD Vance would be attending Burrow on the vice presidential visit to Paycor Stadium: pic.twitter.com/hAktahQopW — Charlie Clifford (@char_cliff) October 21, 2026 Vance, who is from Middletown and owns a home in Cincinnati, once watched the Bengals lose a 2006 playoff game while deployed in Iraq. Now, coming to Burrow, the Bengals QB is dealing with some injuries. In Week 5, when they beat the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium, he jammed his left thumb trying to grab a loose ball. The medical staff checked him out on the sidelines, wrapped his hand up, and Burrow went right back into the game. Before that, in a close 30-27 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3, he got sacked at the 46-yard line with 53 seconds left. But even after losing to the Jacksonville Jaguars the next week, Burrow didn’t panic about the team’s future and kept things in perspective, saying , “We had our opportunities the last two weeks, but certainly this isn’t Armageddon or anything. We’re still in a great spot and feel really good about our team”. Coming off their Week 6 bye, the Bengals resumed practice to regain their footing after losing two of their previous three games. Sitting at 3-2, Cincinnati is currently last in the competitive AFC North. In Week 7’s divisional game, the team will be on the road for a game against the Baltimore Ravens. Gardner-Johnson’s Bizarre On-Field Antics “I’ll Go Get Paid Somewhere Else”: Lions TE Sam Laporta Voices Frustration Over Stalled Contract Talks Shedeur Sanders Drops 4-Word Message On Deion Sanders’ Graphic Foot Photos “NFL is so fake”: Ex-NFL DT calls out league, Robert Saleh over Jordan Elliott gun incident The post Joe Burrow Reacts to JD Vance Visiting Bengals Practice appeared first on Gridiron Heroics .

item.title: By The Numbers: Iowa vs. Minnesota
item.description: Iowa Hawkeyes defensive lineman Jonah Pace (91) and Iowa Hawkeyes defensive lineman Bryce Hawthorne (96) carry the Floyd of Rosedale Trophy after defeating Minnesota Oct. 25, 2025 at Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s been two weeks since Iowa went to Seattle and put down a Washington Huskies team that looked lost for 3 quarters. That game took place just less than 2 weeks after Washington was fairly well dominated (though not so much on the scoreboard) by the Golden Gophers who await them Saturday in Minneapolis. Now, to be fair, Washington surrendered a lot more yardage (especially on the ground) to the Hawks than they did to the Gophers, but Minnesota’s defense put the Huskies into a very similar cage (sorry for all the dog puns, they’re just too easy), allowing just 279 total yards (239 passing, 40 rushing) while intercepting Demond Williams twice. Iowa actually allowed more total yards to the Huskies (317 – 320 passing, -3 rushing) – though a good chunk of that (84 yards) came on the Huskies’ last drive after Iowa’s starters had taken a seat. The difference, really, between Iowa’s win over the Huskies and Minnesota’s win was that Iowa’s offense put on one helluva show. 41 points on 465 total yards (202 passing – 10.6/play, 263 rushing – 6.9/play) was likely not on anyone’s bingo card in a game Iowa entered as a 3.5-point road dog on a West Coast Friday night. Hell, even here at the Pants we, collectively, only had the Hawks putting up 25 points. Minnesota getting taken to the woodshed by OMHR the following day just made the win on the West Coast that much sweeter. So what do we have to look forward to this Saturday in Minneapolis? Well, probably cooler weather, maybe some rain as well, and ideally a return trip to Iowa City for the most beautiful bronze pig anyone has ever laid eyes on. Let’s see what the numbers have to say. Minnesota’s lone win in that 11-game span was 12-10 in Iowa City in 2023. Of note: Iowa has won five straight in Minneapolis (since 2016) Minnesota’s last home win in the series was 51-14 in 2014 Saturday is Minnesota’s Homecoming — the Gophers are 10-4 against Iowa in Homecoming games but haven’t won one since 1974. A Minnesota win would give it Floyd, the Little Brown Jug and Paul Bunyan’s Axe at the same time for the first time since 1978. Iowa currently holds all four of its traveling trophies and is 33-11 in its last 44 rivalry trophy games. item.content:encoded: Iowa Hawkeyes defensive lineman Jonah Pace (91) and Iowa Hawkeyes defensive lineman Bryce Hawthorne (96) carry the Floyd of Rosedale Trophy after defeating Minnesota Oct. 25, 2025 at Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s been two weeks since Iowa went to Seattle and put down a Washington Huskies team that looked lost for 3 quarters. That game took place just less than 2 weeks after Washington was fairly well dominated (though not so much on the scoreboard) by the Golden Gophers who await them Saturday in Minneapolis. Now, to be fair, Washington surrendered a lot more yardage (especially on the ground) to the Hawks than they did to the Gophers, but Minnesota’s defense put the Huskies into a very similar cage (sorry for all the dog puns, they’re just too easy), allowing just 279 total yards (239 passing, 40 rushing) while intercepting Demond Williams twice. Iowa actually allowed more total yards to the Huskies (317 – 320 passing, -3 rushing) – though a good chunk of that (84 yards) came on the Huskies’ last drive after Iowa’s starters had taken a seat. The difference, really, between Iowa’s win over the Huskies and Minnesota’s win was that Iowa’s offense put on one helluva show. 41 points on 465 total yards (202 passing – 10.6/play, 263 rushing – 6.9/play) was likely not on anyone’s bingo card in a game Iowa entered as a 3.5-point road dog on a West Coast Friday night. Hell, even here at the Pants we, collectively, only had the Hawks putting up 25 points. Minnesota getting taken to the woodshed by OMHR the following day just made the win on the West Coast that much sweeter. So what do we have to look forward to this Saturday in Minneapolis? Well, probably cooler weather, maybe some rain as well, and ideally a return trip to Iowa City for the most beautiful bronze pig anyone has ever laid eyes on. Let’s see what the numbers have to say. The Teams Iowa: 5-1 overall, 2-1 conference (No. 15 AP / No. 14 Coaches) Minnesota: 4-2 overall, 2-1 conference Series History All-time record: Minnesota leads 63-54-2 since 1891 — Saturday is the 120th all-time meeting and the 92nd played for Floyd of Rosedale, where Iowa leads 46-43-2 Most recent meeting: Iowa won 41-3 on Oct. 25, 2025, at Kinnick Current streak: Iowa has won 2 straight (2024, 2025), 10 of the last 11 and 20 of the last 25. Minnesota’s lone win in that 11-game span was 12-10 in Iowa City in 2023. Of note: Iowa has won five straight in Minneapolis (since 2016) Minnesota’s last home win in the series was 51-14 in 2014 Saturday is Minnesota’s Homecoming — the Gophers are 10-4 against Iowa in Homecoming games but haven’t won one since 1974. A Minnesota win would give it Floyd, the Little Brown Jug and Paul Bunyan’s Axe at the same time for the first time since 1978. Iowa currently holds all four of its traveling trophies and is 33-11 in its last 44 rivalry trophy games. Coaching Staff Iowa: Kirk Ferentz (28th season; 214-129 at Iowa; 20-7 vs. Minnesota as Iowa’s head coach) / Tim Lester, OC (3rd season) / Phil Parker, DC (15th season) / Chris Polizzi, ST Coordinator (1st season) Minnesota: P.J. Fleck, HC (10th season; 70-46 at Minnesota, 100-68 career; 1-8 vs. Iowa at Minnesota) / Greg Harbaugh Jr., OC (4th season) / Danny Collins, DC (2nd season), with Nick Monroe as co-DC / Daniel Da Prato, ST Coordinator (1st season, from New Mexico). Saturday is the 11th Ferentz–Fleck meeting — the most Fleck has faced any coach. Harbaugh coached WRs at Western Michigan (2020-21) under Lester, who succeeded Fleck there. Offense Total YPG Passing YPG Rushing YPG PPG Iowa 403.2 209.2 194.0 31.0 Minnesota 341.3 236.5 104.8 28.8 Jeremy Hecklinski is your starting QB, at least for one more week. It’s not all that surprising given that Hank wasn’t 100% going into the game against Washington (medically cleared or not), so it would make sense that Heck would get the majority of snaps with the 1’s last week during the by, and most likely the majority of snaps starting last Sunday. Yes, Kirk has confirmed that Hank is 100%, but he hasn’t been at full strength since about halfway through the 4th quarter of the OSU game, so why wouldn’t they stick with the hot hand. Regardless of who is taking the snaps, Kamari Moulton is definitely at 100% and will be hungry for another 100+ yard game as he pushes closer and closer to his first 1000-yard rushing season, and he’ll be going up against a Minnesota Oline that allowed Purdue to rush for more than 300 yards two weeks ago. Oh, not to mention that LJ Phillips is fully back from tweaking his ankle against the Huskies, and Braden Jackson is still super duper fast. Minnesota has weapons to be sure – Javon Tracy, Noah Jennings, and Jalen Smith are all averaging more than 11.5 yards per catch, and TJ Thomas (if he’s healthy) is averaging 6.2 yards per carry. They also have an experienced QB in Drake Lindsay, though his 5 INTs this season (to 9 TDs) may belie that experience. This one probably won’t be easy, but I’ll be honest, I like the way this team is playing right now, especially with Heck under center. He brings an edge that Hank just doesn’t seem to have, and I think they are hitting their stride at exactly the right time. ADVANTAGE: Iowa — ~62 more yards per game, driven by a run game that’s 35th nationally (6.1 per carry, 3rd in FBS) against Minnesota’s 129th (3.66 per carry). Minnesota throws for 27 more yards a game, and both lines protect well: Iowa has allowed 5 sacks (10th in FBS), Minnesota 4 (9th). Defense Total YPG Allowed Passing YPG Allowed Rushing YPG Allowed PPG Allowed Iowa 293.3 208.7 84.7 14.5 Minnesota 288.8 159.7 129.2 21.8 Let’s recap the Iowa’s defenses performance in the first half last week: Punt, Punt, Punt, Punt, Punt, FG, end of half. Washington’s total yards at halftime? 109. First downs? 7. Points? 3. That’s one helluva half from a unit that was reeling a little bit after getting beat up by OSU. They did struggle a little out of the half, but to hold a P4 opponent to negative rushing yards is nothing to sniff at. Yeah, there were some issues in the secondary when UW decided to bring in a QB that actually wanted to play in the game, and some penalties that cost them some yards, but on balance, there wasn’t a whole lot to be unhappy about with the defense’s performance against the Huskies. Minnesota’s defense, on the other hand, had a terrible, horrible, no good, very bad day two Saturdays ago in West Lafayette. It should be said that prior to that shellacking, they had put up some pretty solid numbers across their first 5 weeks. They’re 18th in scoring defense, top 10 against the pass, and averaging more than 7 TFLs per game. They may not be elite, but they are still pretty good. But again, they gave up 41 to Purdue two weeks ago, so I guess it’s all going to come down to which version of the Minnesota defense shows up. ADVANTAGE: Iowa — 8th nationally in scoring defense, 7th against the run (2.5 per carry, one rushing TD allowed all season) and 6th in sacks (3.17 per game). Minnesota’s defense is better than its scoring average suggests, but it’s 104th in red-zone defense (88.9% scoring rate). Special Teams Punt Avg FG% Kick Return Avg Punt Return Avg Iowa 43.0 (net 41.4) 81.8% (9-11) 41.5 13.4 Minnesota 40.9 (net 39.6) 100% (11-11) 21.7 18.1 Iowa’s special teams have been quite impressive in 2026, and it’s even more impressive given what they had to replace after 2025. Boston Everitt is a huge part of that equation (and arguably an upgrade over Rhys Dakin). We haven’t replaced Kaden Wetjen (though no one seems to want to do anything to allow kick or punt returns this season), but Evan James and RVZ have done a more than serviceable job handling punts, and Braden is always a threat to put up a good kickoff return (provided he can field one). All in all, it’s reassuring that what looked like it could be a weakness going into the season has proved to be an immutable strength for the Hawks. Minnesota ain’t t

item.title: ‘(Pat) McAfee Experience Is Coming to a Conclusion,’ ‘Showing Some Cracks’ — NFL Fans React As ESPN Star’s MNF Alt-Cast Gets Beat by ManningCast
item.description: ‘(Pat) McAfee Experience Is Coming to a Conclusion,’ ‘Showing Some Cracks’ — NFL Fans React As ESPN Star’s MNF Alt-Cast Gets Beat by ManningCast Pat McAfee brought his alt-cast to “Monday Night Football” for the first time on Oct. 19. “Monday Night Football Field Pass with The Pat McAfee Show” debuted on ESPN2 during the San Francisco 49ers’ 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders. However, the debut drew 351,000 viewers, according to a source cited by The Athletic’s Andrew Marchand. ESPN declined to confirm the figure, “which is not common practice,” Marchand wrote. Some fans read the number as a sign of McAfee fatigue catching up with the former Indianapolis Colts punter. How Pat McAfee’s Debut Stacked Up Against the Other Alt-Casts In its Oct. 11 announcement, ESPN said the show would bring “its high-energy, free-flowing commentary and sideline-driven approach” to the NFL. The announcement placed McAfee behind an end zone with Dan Orlovsky and Darius Butler and put Connor Campbell, Ty Schmit and Tone Digs in a suite inside the stadium. Commanders-49ers was the first of five “Monday Night Football” editions. After those come a Week 18 Saturday game and a Super Bowl 61 edition on ESPNU on Feb. 14. Marchand compared the debut with Peyton and Eli Manning’s “ManningCast,” reporting that McAfee’s audience was “around half of what the Mannings have received.” So did McAfee lose a head-to-head fight with the Mannings? No. The two shows did not air against each other. McAfee’s “Monday Night Football” alt-cast only airs during selected weeks when the “ManningCast” is not airing. The alt-cast that did air against him was “MNF Playbook with Next Gen Stats,” ESPN’s data and analytics show on NFL Network. Monday was its second “Monday Night Football” appearance of the season. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Sports Business Journal reporter Austin Karp published a breakdown that matched Marchand’s ESPN2 figure, showing McAfee was “actually outdrawn.” The Next Gen Stats telecast drew 469,000 viewers, 118,000 more than McAfee by Karp’s numbers. The game itself drew 6.688 million viewers on ESPN and 10.312 million on the ABC simulcast. For comparison, the ManningCast drew 705,000 viewers for its Week 1 Chiefs-Broncos broadcast and 661,000 in Week 2. NFL Fans See Signs of McAfee Fatigue One fan wrote , “One can only hope the McAfee experience is coming to a conclusion.” Another fan suggested that “the oversaturation of McAfee may be finally showing some cracks,” adding, “Like his style in small doses he’s everywhere now.” McAfee is on ESPN even more this season. He currently also holds a full-time role on “Monday Night Countdown,” the network’s pregame and halftime show. That comes on top of his central spot on “College GameDay” and the daily afternoon show ESPN licenses from him. Another fan put it more bluntly : “America has McAfee fatigue. His employer just hasn’t figured it out yet.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Pred

item.title: INTERVIEW | Charlie Cresswell on Rennes’ Europa League goals: ‘There are no limits.’
item.description: INTERVIEW | Charlie Cresswell on Rennes’ Europa League goals: ‘There are no limits.’ Stade Rennais head to Turin tonight in what is their biggest challenge so far in this season’s UEFA Europa League. Thus far, Rennes have one win and one draw in the competition. Speaking to Get French Football News, Charlie Cresswell (23) outlined the Breton club’s objectives in the competition. The former England youth international said that participating in European competition was part of the draw at Rennes. Tonight’s match against Juventus is the highlight fixture in their ‘League Phase’ draw. Speaking ahead of it, Cresswell outlined the objectives. “There are no limits. It would be stupid to put limits on ourselves. We can say we can win it.” He added, “[We have] such a good team here, good staff. Yeah, it’d be stupid to put limits on ourselves. ” In what is the first European campaign of Cresswell’s young career, he is not just there to make up the numbers. >> Read our piece in partnership with The Guardian HERE GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Week 7 TNF Fantasy Football Wide Receiver Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: A.J. Brown vs. Luther Burden
item.description: Oct 18, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) runs with the ball after a catch in the second quarter against the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Heading into Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season, fantasy football managers are still dealing with an ever-evolving running back landscape, as well as ongoing bye weeks. With the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears facing each other on Thursday Night Football, this week presents us with an interesting Start/Sit decision between two stud wide receivers: New England's A.J. Brown and Chicago's Luther Burden III. Let's break down both players' recent play, matchup dynamics, and injury news in this Week 7 Thursday Night Football Wide Receiver Start 'Em, Sit 'Em debate. item.title: Cardinals’ 5-Year Veteran Draws Interest From Astros
item.description: ST. LOUIS, MO - MAY 23: Relief pitcher Randy Flores #34 of the St. Louis Cardinals throws against the Pittsburgh Pirates on May 23, 2007 at Busch Stadium in St. Louis, Missouri. The Cards beat the Pirates 5-3. (Photo by Dilip Vishwanat/Getty Images) Getty Images The St. Louis Cardinals enter the offseason with reason to believe their rebuilding process is beginning to pay off. Though they missed the playoffs this season, the organization has identified several young players who could form the foundation of its next competitive team. Now, the front office faces another challenge: continuing to develop that talent while making decisions that could shape the club’s direction for years to come. “The Cardinals overachieved in a rebuilding year and also learned who some of their long-term pieces are, from JJ Wetherholt to Jordan Walker to Joshua Baez to Leo Bernal,” Will Leitch wrote for MLB.com . “This team will be contending, and likely soon. This offseason provides a fascinating opportunity, then.” While much of the attention will center on roster upgrades and player development, the Cardinals could also face an important question about its leadership group. One member of the organization’s front office who is also a veteran of the team’s pitching staff has reportedly attracted interest from a team looking to fill its own key executive position. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Yankees Castoff Joins Hated Rival Immediate After Season Ends St Louis Cardinals Veteran Draws Houston Astros Interest Cardinals assistant general manager Randy Flores is among the candidates who have drawn serious interest from the Houston Astros as they search for a new general manager. “Longtime Milwaukee Brewers executive Matt Kleine, Chicago White Sox assistant general manager Josh Barfield, Kansas City Royals senior vice president Scott Sharp, Atlanta Braves assistant general manager Ben Sestanovich and St. Louis Cardinals assistant general manager Randy Flores are among the candidates who have drawn serious interest from the Astros,” according to The Athletic’s Chandler Rome . Flores has a history with the Cardinals that extends beyond his current front-office role. The former southpaw pitched for the Cardinals from 2004 to 2008, winning a World Series with the team in 2006. “Flores played in parts of eight major league seasons from 2002-10,” Steve Adams wrote for MLB Trade Rumors . “The former ninth-round pick had a few strong seasons as a left-handed reliever, primarily for the same Cardinals that now employ him as an executive.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Trump Sends 2-Word Jab At Brewers, Rays MLB World Series Matchup What St Louis Cardinals World Series Champion’s Potential Houston Astros Move Could Mean Flores’ experience as both a former player and an executive should make him an appealing candidate for Houston. The Astros are seeking leadership for their baseball operations department, while Flores has been involved in the Cardinals’ efforts to build a younger roster.

item.title: JJ McCarthy makes NFL history in comeback effort against the Giants
item.description: UTBP/Depositphotos Ringo Chiu/Shutterstock.com McCarthy’s 243-yard performance puts Giants’ quarterback plans in focus J.J. McCarthy delivered a remarkable fourth-quarter performance against the New Orleans Saints on October 18, 2026, throwing for 243 yards after replacing Jameis Winston at quarterback. The New York Giants faced a 24-point deficit but mounted a late rally that brought them within one score of tying the game. Despite McCarthy’s passing production and 17 unanswered points, New York fell 34–27. On October 21, head coach John Harbaugh named McCarthy the Giants’ starting quarterback for their Week 7 game against the Houston Texans. Steve Jacobson/Shutterstock.com The Giants turn to McCarthy New York started Jameis Winston at quarterback against New Orleans at MetLife Stadium. Winston threw two interceptions, including one early in the fourth quarter, before coach John Harbaugh replaced him with McCarthy. The Giants trailed 34–10 when the quarterback change occurred. McCarthy entered with limited time remaining and immediately faced the challenge of moving the offense against a sizable deficit. bellafotosolo/Depositphotos New York faces a 24-point deficit The Saints built a 34–10 lead after taking control of the game following New York’s early advantage. Chris Olave caught an 18-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough early in the fourth quarter to extend New Orleans’ lead. With the Giants trailing by 24 points, J.J. McCarthy replaced Jameis Winston at quarterback. New York needed multiple scoring drives and defensive stops to have a chance of changing the result. Depositphotos McCarthy starts with an interception McCarthy’s first appearance for the Giants did not begin smoothly, as he threw an interception on his first possession. The turnover added an early setback while New York attempted to close the gap against New Orleans. However, McCarthy continued directing the offense after the mistake. He threw for 243 yards and a touchdown in just over 11 minutes, helping the Giants mount a late comeback before their 34–27 defeat. Depositphotos The Giants begin scoring again New York began its late scoring surge when Tyrone Tracy Jr. scored a rushing touchdown with about seven minutes remaining. McCarthy helped the Giants move the ball as they attempted to cut into the Saints’ lead. The two-point conversion succeeded on a pass from McCarthy to tight end Isaiah Likely. The play reduced New Orleans’ advantage to 34–18 and kept the Giants within reach of a closer finish. noonie/Depositphotos McCarthy connects with Isaiah Likely McCarthy followed the Giants’ first touchdown with another scoring drive against the Saints. He connected with Isaiah Likely for a touchdown pass during the fourth quarter as New York continued its comeback attempt. The Giants attempted a two-point conversion after the score but did not convert. The touchdown brought New York closer to the Saints, although the Giants still needed additional points to complete the comeback
item.content:encoded: UTBP/Depositphotos Ringo Chiu/Shutterstock.com McCarthy’s 243-yard performance puts Giants’ quarterback plans in focus J.J. McCarthy delivered a remarkable fourth-quarter performance against the New Orleans Saints on October 18, 2026, throwing for 243 yards after replacing Jameis Winston at quarterback. The New York Giants faced a 24-point deficit but mounted a late rally that brought them within one score of tying the game. Despite McCarthy’s passing production and 17 unanswered points, New York fell 34–27. On October 21, head coach John Harbaugh named McCarthy the Giants’ starting quarterback for their Week 7 game against the Houston Texans. Steve Jacobson/Shutterstock.com The Giants turn to McCarthy New York started Jameis Winston at quarterback against New Orleans at MetLife Stadium. Winston threw two interceptions, including one early in the fourth quarter, before coach John Harbaugh replaced him with McCarthy. The Giants trailed 34–10 when the quarterback change occurred. McCarthy entered with limited time remaining and immediately faced the challenge of moving the offense against a sizable deficit. bellafotosolo/Depositphotos New York faces a 24-point deficit The Saints built a 34–10 lead after taking control of the game following New York’s early advantage. Chris Olave caught an 18-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough early in the fourth quarter to extend New Orleans’ lead. With the Giants trailing by 24 points, J.J. McCarthy replaced Jameis Winston at quarterback. New York needed multiple scoring drives and defensive stops to have a chance of changing the result. Depositphotos McCarthy starts with an interception McCarthy’s first appearance for the Giants did not begin smoothly, as he threw an interception on his first possession. The turnover added an early setback while New York attempted to close the gap against New Orleans. However, McCarthy continued directing the offense after the mistake. He threw for 243 yards and a touchdown in just over 11 minutes, helping the Giants mount a late comeback before their 34–27 defeat. Depositphotos The Giants begin scoring again New York began its late scoring surge when Tyrone Tracy Jr. scored a rushing touchdown with about seven minutes remaining. McCarthy helped the Giants move the ball as they attempted to cut into the Saints’ lead. The two-point conversion succeeded on a pass from McCarthy to tight end Isaiah Likely. The play reduced New Orleans’ advantage to 34–18 and kept the Giants within reach of a closer finish. noonie/Depositphotos McCarthy connects with Isaiah Likely McCarthy followed the Giants’ first touchdown with another scoring drive against the Saints. He connected with Isaiah Likely for a touchdown pass during the fourth quarter as New York continued its comeback attempt. The Giants attempted a two-point conversion after the score but did not convert. The touchdown brought New York closer to the Saints, although the Giants still needed additional points to complete the comeback. bellafotosolo/Depositphotos A record-tying 243 passing yards McCarthy accumulated 243 passing yards during his fourth-quarter appearance against New Orleans. He produced that total in 11 minutes and 25 seconds after replacing Jameis Winston. Despite throwing an interception on his first possession, McCarthy then led three scoring drives. His 243 passing yards tied the Giants’ highest single-quarter total since at least 1991, and New York cut a 24-point deficit to 7 before losing 34–27. Debby Wong/Shutterstock.com McCarthy matches a Giants franchise mark McCarthy’s 243 passing yards were the second-most by a Giants quarterback in a fourth quarter. Eli Manning threw for 254 yards in the fourth quarter of a 36–25 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on October 9, 2011. McCarthy also matched Manning’s 243-yard fourth quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2012. McCarthy produced his total in 11 minutes and 25 seconds after entering with New York trailing 34–10. Although the Giants lost 34–27, his late passing helped bring them within one score of the Saints. Interesting fact : McCarthy was the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. actionsports/Depositphotos Malik Nabers contributes to the offense Wide receiver Malik Nabers played an important role in the Giants’ passing attack against New Orleans. He recorded 12 receptions for 165 yards, making him one of the game’s leading receiving contributors. Nabers’ production helped New York move the ball against the Saints. His performance also formed part of the wider evaluation of the Giants’ offense following the 34–27 defeat and McCarthy’s late appearance at quarterback. bellafotosolo/Depositphotos Likely provides another receiving option Tight end Isaiah Likely contributed to New York’s offensive production against the Saints. He recorded six receptions for 99 yards and a touchdown, including a fourth-quarter scoring catch from McCarthy. Likely’s involvement gave the Giants another productive option in the passing game. His touchdown helped New York continue its rally, although the offense ultimately failed to complete the comeback. noonie/Depositphotos The Giants score 17 unanswered points New York scored 17 unanswered points in the final 11 minutes of its game against the Saints. The late surge included Tyrone Tracy Jr.’s rushing touchdown, McCarthy’s touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely and a field goal by Dominic Zvada. The Giants’ defense also forced a turnover and three punts during the comeback attempt. Despite those contributions, New York remained seven points behind in the closing seconds and ultimately lost 34–27. UTBP/Depositphotos The comeback ends on fourth down The Giants had one final opportunity to tie the game in the closing seconds. Facing fourth-and-one at the Saints’ 14-yard line with 12 seconds remaining, McCarthy threw a pass intended for Likely in the back of the end zone. The pass fell incomplete, ending New York’s comeback attempt. The Saints held on for a 34–27 victory after allowing the Giants to score 17 unanswered points during the final 11 minutes. A confrontation involving a stadium worker has brought attention to the interactions surrounding the Dallas Cowboys quarterback. Find out why Michael Irvin pointed to Dak Prescott’s role in the stadium worker confrontation . katatonia82/Depositphotos McCarthy’s performance raises quarterback questions McCarthy’s fourth-quarter production led the Giants to reconsider their quarterback plan for Week 7. On October 19, head coach John Harbaugh said the team was still choosing between McCarthy and Winston for its October 25 game against the Houston Texans. On October 21, Harbaugh announced that McCarthy would start in Houston, with Winston serving as the backup. Winston finished the Saints game with 152 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception. A costly play by the New York Giants running back became a talking point after the matchup with Washington. Discover why Mike Tomlin criticized Cam Skattebo’s mistake against the Commanders . What do you think about McCarthy’s performance, and should he start the Giants’ next game? Like this post and share your thoughts in the comments! This slideshow was made with AI assistance and human editing. item.title: Manuel Neuer won’t cry after Bayern Munich allows late goal to Arsenal in 2-2 draw
item.description: (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) | Getty Images Manuel Neuer believes Bayern Munich can take some positives from their 2-2 draw with Arsenal, despite the frustration of conceding a late equalizer. The Bayern captain acknowledged that both sides were evenly matched on the nig ht and felt the result was ultimately fair, even if the manner in which Bayern surrendered their lead left a bitter ta ste. “It was a game at an equal level. Of course, it’s annoying to concede the equalizer at the end of the g ame, but I think it’s an okay result,” Neuer said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). Neuer also made it clear that Bayern Munich cannot afford to dwell on the dropped points, with several important Champions League fixtures still ahead. Away trips to Atlético Madrid and Lille will prese nt significant challenges, while Bayern must take advantage of their home matches if they want to strength en their position in the competition . “We still have some tough fixtures like Atlético Madrid and Lille away. We also have home games where we should be expected to win. We just have to do our homework in the coming weeks,” Neuer said. The message from Neuer is straightforward: Bayern have put themselves in a position to compete, but they must deliver consistently over the coming weeks. The draw against Arsenal is not a disaster, but Bayern will need to turn solid performances into victorie s if they want to make their ambitions a reality. Join the conversation! item.title: The NFC East offers a turnaround chance for one struggling team - Daily Slop
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders looks to pass against the Philadelphia Eagles in the first quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 22 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Riggo’s Rag Commanders’ bleak start hides a playoff opening that’s still within reach Even with the second-worst record in the conference, the Commanders are only two games out of first place in their division. And if the team makes the necessary adjustments over their week off , that deficit could shrink quickly. When the Commanders return to the field, they’ll play the Philadelphia Eagles at home without quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is done for the year with a scary blood clot situation. After that, they’ll play the biggest disappointment in the NFL — with the only possible exception of the team they share a stadium with — the Los Angeles Rams. If the Commanders win both of those games, they’re right back in business. And it’ll only get better from there. They’ll face the New York Giants on the road, who they should’ve beaten at home . They’ll host the ever-inconsistent Cincinnati Bengals. They’ll visit the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans, two teams they should beat regardless of the location. Then they’ll host the Houston Texans and Atlanta Falcons, both currently sub-.500 operations. The Commanders should win at least five of those games. They can probably win all of them if they bring their best. [U]n 2020, Washington started the season 2-7 and rallied to make the playoffs at 7-9. This Commanders team is substantially more talented than that one was. That squad’s regular-season quarterbacks were Dwayne Haskins, Kyle Allen, and a one-legged Alex Smith. Its second-leading receiver was Cam Sims. This team has Jayden Daniels under center. Even without McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, third-round rookie Antonio Williams, and Treylon Burks are still here. And first-year linebacker Sonny Styles is putting together a Defensive Rookie of the Year-caliber campaign just as Chase Young did then . Did a bit of a deep dive on Jayden Daniels stats after his impressive second half in San Fran. Jayden Daniels has played in 31 games (including 3 playoff games) in his career. That doesn’t even come out to 2 full seasons. Jayden Daniels career stats (including playoffs):… — Alex Flum (@AlexFlumTV) October 20, 2026 All the Commanders need to do is stay relatively healthy the rest of the way and let the rest of the NFC East keep imploding. Once they pick up one or two wins, which they’d better be able to do with this stretch coming up, they’ll have momentum and vibes on their side.

To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Adj comp pct rate takes into account the number of aimed passes that are on target pic.twitter.com/cB0Mv76opx — PFF (@PFF) October 22, 2026 Sports Illustrated With Terry McLaurin Out, Washington Must Change How It Uses Antonio Williams [T]he reason they need to give him more looks is clear: he creates separation like no one else on the roster, and even though his snap share has stayed steady (hovering in the high 60s of late, even in London when McLaurin was out nursing a hamstring), he’s criminally underused in David Blough’s system. Against San Francisco, Williams ran 35 routes but had only four targets, catching three for 50 yards. All four targets came on third down in the fourth quarter, and his three catches accounted for Washington’s only successful third-down conversions of the night. In an offense looking for answers, why ignore one? Jayden Daniels with big-time throws to Terry McLaurin, Chig Okonkwo, Antonio Williams, and Treylon Burks. Nice play designs and some "interesting" coverage from the 49ers. pic.twitter.com/oBEO0JORHu — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) October 21, 2026 A glance over Williams’ numbers above makes a major case for him to be involved earlier and more often, including plays where he’s the intended first read. PFF credits him with 69 run-blocking snaps and a 51.5 run-blocking grade, leaving room for improvement if Washington expands his role in two-receiver formations. The bye gives Blough time to make Williams a bigger part of the plan from the opening drive. Give him designed opportunities on first and second down. item.title: Strength in Variety: How Mizzou’s frontcourt protects the paint by committee
item.description: Before teaming up at Missouri, transfers Bryson Tiller, right, and Jaylen Carey, left, battled at the Players Era Festival in Las Vegas last November. | Getty Images Under coach Dennis Gates, patience defined Missouri’s search for a center. When the transfer portal opened, the Tigers’ staff devoted early resources elsewhere to shore up or reboot their roster. Then, usually in late April or May, the program would rummage around for an affordable veteran, a process that turned up the likes of Connor Vanover, Josh Gray or Shawn Phillips Jr. At the same time, MU might take a swing on a project like Jordan Butler, Peyton Marshall or Trent Burns. Four years in, neither approach has cultivated much continuity. So, Gates changed tack this spring. He moved swiftly to secure Jaylen Carey as a rugged depth piece and committed real resources to mining Bryson Tiller’s upside. Meanwhile, MU kept Burns in the fold rather than abandoning the developmental route. Ideally, Tiller makes the pecking order easy by claiming the bulk of the minutes. But with Carey and Burns on hand, Gates has some latitude to tailor the job rather than ask one player to handle everything. And that’s useful because operating at center involves more than occupying the lane and waiting to contest a shot. Often, the job starts when something goes wrong farther from the basket. As we’ve noted before , tMU’s late-season slide wasn’t tied to a lack of size. The trouble started on the ball. The Tigers couldn’t consistently prevent guards and wings from turning the corner, forcing the back line to absorb one breakdown after another. Eventually, it couldn’t plug every leak. Starting in late January, the results around the rim made that clear. View Link At least Gates has more ways to handle that pressure. Bryson Tiller, Jaylen Carey and Trent Burns bring different tools to the job, giving MU some flexibility in how it protects the paint. There’s a catch, though. None carried a starter’s workload at center last season. As a group, they averaged slightly more than 16 minutes per game, operating as clear backups or deep-bench options. Their court time was relatively consistent, but hardly extensive. View Link Does that mean a larger burden is beyond them? Not necessarily. But we’re dealing with projections, not proof. In previous seasons, Gates’ scheduling philosophy might have afforded more time to tinker and sort out the rotation. This campaign won’t afford the same luxury. Still, scattered throughout those modest minutes are clues about what each player might provide — and, just as importantly, what Gates would need to put around him to make it work. item.content:encoded: Before teaming up at Missouri, transfers Bryson Tiller, right, and Jaylen Carey, left, battled at the Players Era Festival in Las Vegas last November. | Getty Images Under coach Dennis Gates, patience defined Missouri’s search for a center. When the transfer portal opened, the Tigers’ staff devoted early resources elsewhere to shore up or reboot their roster. Then, usually in late April or May, the program would rummage around for an affordable veteran, a process that turned up the likes of Connor Vanover, Josh Gray or Shawn Phillips Jr. At the same time, MU might take a swing on a project like Jordan Butler, Peyton Marshall or Trent Burns. Four years in, neither approach has cultivated much continuity. So, Gates changed tack this spring. He moved swiftly to secure Jaylen Carey as a rugged depth piece and committed real resources to mining Bryson Tiller’s upside. Meanwhile, MU kept Burns in the fold rather than abandoning the developmental route. Ideally, Tiller makes the pecking order easy by claiming the bulk of the minutes. But with Carey and Burns on hand, Gates has some latitude to tailor the job rather than ask one player to handle everything. And that’s useful because operating at center involves more than occupying the lane and waiting to contest a shot. Often, the job starts when something goes wrong farther from the basket. As we’ve noted before , tMU’s late-season slide wasn’t tied to a lack of size. The trouble started on the ball. The Tigers couldn’t consistently prevent guards and wings from turning the corner, forcing the back line to absorb one breakdown after another. Eventually, it couldn’t plug every leak. Starting in late January, the results around the rim made that clear. View Link At least Gates has more ways to handle that pressure. Bryson Tiller, Jaylen Carey and Trent Burns bring different tools to the job, giving MU some flexibility in how it protects the paint. There’s a catch, though. None carried a starter’s workload at center last season. As a group, they averaged slightly more than 16 minutes per game, operating as clear backups or deep-bench options. Their court time was relatively consistent, but hardly extensive. View Link Does that mean a larger burden is beyond them? Not necessarily. But we’re dealing with projections, not proof. In previous seasons, Gates’ scheduling philosophy might have afforded more time to tinker and sort out the rotation. This campaign won’t afford the same luxury. Still, scattered throughout those modest minutes are clues about what each player might provide — and, just as importantly, what Gates would need to put around him to make it work. Bryson Tiller: Versatility — With a Tradeoff The last time Tiller saw extended time at the five, it overlapped with four minutes as Houston began to pull away in the Big 12 Tournament semifinal. JoJo Tugler walled off the redshirt freshman from a Mercy Miller drive, then backed him down and spun around a wall-up for an easy bucket. The next trip, Tiller reacted late to Chris Cenac flashing to the mid-post for a soft jumper. But that sequence didn’t raise Kansas coach Bill Self’s ire. Barely two minutes in, Tiller let Tugler collect a miss despite having an ideal box-out position. Self immediately called a timeout. At halftime, he pulled Tiller. “Well, my message is to rebound and play competitive,” Self said afterward . “That’s it. Be physical, rebound, play competitive. … It’s been the message for a long time.” That withering assessment, at least to the west, has shaped the final impression of Tiller’s stint in Lawrence. Reducing Tiller’s profile to physicality and rebounding obscures another reality: Self never stopped experimenting with him at center. Tiller appeared there in every game but one, logged at least five minutes in 22 and routinely served as the lone interior player surrounded by four nominal guards or wings. There’s zero point hiding that the results were terrible. Core lineup combinations with Tiller in the post were strafed for a 118.3 raw defensive rating, per EvanMiya.com, a trend mirrored in games where he received his standard allotment at the five. View Link Yet the tape isn’t a gaffe reel. Our charting identified Tiller as the source of just one primary advantage, while 27 of 30 shots were, at minimum, lightly contested. So how did Tiller wind up linked with such putrid outcomes? Reviewing season-long data also deepens the contradiction. Tiller surrendered 0.813 PPP and ranked in the 74th percentile nationally, per Synergy Sports, while conceding just 0.713 PPP as the terminal defender of ball screens, isolations and post-ups. The tools ($) explain why. Tiller flips his hips, maintains cushion, recovers with length and can survive switches or crossmatches that might sink other bigs. But look at what happened when he logged his minutes as the sole big. That leaves a frustrating paradox: If Tiller can handle those jobs, why is the accounting so poor? View Link Exploring Tiller’s switching starts to untangle the wires. With him at center, it was treated as an automatic decision to counteract a ball screen. It could snuff out the initial advantage, but at a cost: Tiller left the lane. Tre White slid down from the wing to slot in as a small-ball four, yet rarely replaced him as the low man. Self’s group instead relied heavily on weak-side rotations. Watch the packet twice. The first viewing demonstrates that Tiller is more than functional in space. On the second, watch how KU organizes itself behind him. Frequently, the possession’s success has little to do with Tiller. Charting those possessions made rim replacement the loudest structural signal. When the rim remained protected, Kansas usually survived. When it didn’t, every possession in the sample ended in a score. Tiller’s versatility only worked if somebody else picked up his shift in the lane. The second clip provides a textbook illustration. Tiller catch-hedges Cayden Boozer, but White doesn’t fully recover and essentially passes off the job to Tiller in a late switch. The sequence saddles Tiller with two poor choices: commit to Boozer and permit an easy drop-off pass or continue to give cushion. Ultimately, Boozer keeps his pace, uses the rim as a shield and converts. Unfortunately, not every breach can be traced to the scheme. Sometimes Tiller was the last line of defense and, as Self pointed out, didn’t act like one. The miscues vary — a passive wall-up, a missed rotation, positioning a step too high above the restricted area — but the first cut-up shows Tiller can do the job. Consistency is the next step. That’s even more apparent when you study Tiller’s handiwork guarding post-ups. Our charted film set captured four examples, and they resulted in just one point. In some ways, Self’s frustration is easy to understand. Tiller doesn’t sweat absorbing contact, contesting vertically and allowing off-ball help to rotate. And any issues rarely stemmed from an opposing center simply displacing him For MU, lessening some of the structural strain starts by surrounding Tiller with more positional size. Carey, Burns, Mark Mitchell and Toni Bryant provide it, and even a four-guard alignment could feature a bigger wing like Trent Pierce. That matters on the glass, too. At Kansas, Tiller was often pulled outside optimal rebounding position. For example, our diagnostic sample contained 12 rebound opportunities, and only two were solely Tiller’s responsibility. (He secured both.) Yes, he can be more assertive, but lineup construction matters. The subtler question is how frequently MU switches with Tiller. At pro day, its default ball-screen coverage asked bigs to play at the level or softly hedge, with switches used more selectively. Its off-ball defenders also sit near the midline, positioning them to help aggressively behind the action. None of that magically turns Tiller into a backline anchor.
