item.title: I'm serious about getting England call - Hendy
item.description: George Hendy has scored 44 tries in 80 games for Northampton so far [Getty Images] Northampton back George Hendy says he is determined to force his way into England contention, with next month's Nations Championship matches fast approaching. Hendy has been one of the Saints' form players over the past few seasons, making match-winning contributions in the Prem final victories in 2024 and 2026. But while a host of club-mates have become regulars for their country, the 24-year-old has had to bide his time. "I just want to throw my hat in the ring for England and I'm really quite serious about that," Hendy told BBC Sport. "Whether that's on the wing or at 15, whatever gives me the best opportunity to get into that squad, I want to take it, and I am pretty happy with the direction I am going in." Northampton 'security incident' believed to be a hoax Saracens in talks over Itoje extension Smith set for Quins landmark as Baxter returns England boss Steve Borthwick will name a training squad on Sunday in preparation for the November leg of the Nations Championship. Borthwick's side recovered from a chastening Six Nations to win two of their three summer matches, and now welcome Australia, Japan and New Zealand to London before the finals weekend at the end of the month. A unique talent with the ball in hand, Hendy says he has been working hard at all parts of his game after conversations with the England management. "I've known for a while what my work-ons are and it feels like the penny's finally dropping," he added. "I think my USP is being able to beat defenders and being able to finish tries. And just because I'm working on other things doesn't mean I stop working on that, so I know that if I keep doing that stuff ball in hand whilst touching up the other aspects of my game I'll be in a pretty good spot. "I've had a few [conversations with the England coaches]. Myself and the Saints coaches know exactly what I need to do to kick on to that next level and all I can do is do that on the weekends." Hendy says he is inspired by the example of his Northampton team-mates, with Fin Smith, Tommy Freeman, Alex Coles, Alex Mitchell, Henry Pollock and Fraser Dingwall among those to become England stalwarts. "That makes me want it even more, I think, seeing your mates going and putting on an England shirt and doing what they love doing and representing their country," Hendy said. "And then you get to see them and you're hearing all about the stories. I just want to be a part of that as well. "I know that with them in camp, it'll be a good environment. item.title: Caleb Williams sends Patriots warning with major NFL honor before Thursday Night Football
item.description: Caleb Williams sends Patriots warning with major NFL honor before Thursday Night Football originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots have won three consecutive games and enter Thursday Night Football with considerable momentum. Unfortunately for New England, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams might be playing his best football at exactly the wrong time. Williams was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week following an impressive performance against the Atlanta Falcons . The former No. 1 overall draft pick completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown in Chicago's victory. He finished with a 111.2 passer rating, delivering one of the most efficient performances of his young career. The recognition came after Williams missed three consecutive games because of a hamstring injury. His return could hardly have been more encouraging for Chicago. Now he prepares to face Drake Maye and the Patriots in a nationally televised matchup between two teams with identical 4-2 records. Williams delivers remarkable comeback performance Williams' performance against Atlanta was notable for several reasons. His 83.3% completion percentage represented a career-best mark, while his 305 passing yards marked his first 300-yard game of the season. Caleb Williams won Week 6 NFC Player of The Week! -30/36 -83.3 CMP % -305 Passing Yards -1 TD -0 INT -111.2 RTG Great to have QB1 back https://t.co/kzZc8bfOuN — Just Another Year Chicago: Bears (@JAYChi_Bears) October 21, 2026 Chicago also demonstrated impressive efficiency near the goal line, scoring on four of its five red-zone opportunities before accounting for a final possession that ended with kneel-downs. The performance earned Williams his second career NFC Offensive Player of the Week award. He joined Jay Cutler as the only Bears quarterbacks to receive the honor twice. That distinction illustrates the significance of his latest performance. Williams also became only the second NFL quarterback this season to complete more than 80% of his passes while throwing for at least 300 yards on 35 or more attempts. Geno Smith accomplished the feat earlier in the season. For Chicago, the performance reinforced the importance of having its starting quarterback healthy again. New England has allowed just 18.8 points per game through its first six contests, helping the Patriots establish themselves as one of the AFC's more competitive teams. However, maintaining that defensive production against Chicago could require contributions from several replacement players. Maye has also been impressive recently. Their careers will inevitably invite comparisons because of their shared draft class. For now, Williams has the latest individual recognition. Maye has the opportunity to help New England extend its winning streak. The Patriots and Bears kick off Thursday at 8:15 p.m. ET at Soldier Field. With both teams holding winning records and their quarterbacks playing well, the matchup could become one of Week 7's most entertaining games. item.title: Patrick Mahomes Sounds Alarm on Jalen Hurts Health Scare in NFL
item.description: Patrick Mahomes has kept his focus sharp this season. The Chiefs improved to 5-0 after a 22-6 win over the Chargers on Sunday, and the quarterback now has a lot to say off the field. His latest comments address a serious health scare involving fellow Eagles star Jalen Hurts , and they carry real weight around the league. Patrick Mahomes Sounds Alarm on Jalen Hurts Health Scare in NFL Mahomes addressed the situation on 96.5 The Fan podcast after the Eagles confirmed that Jalen Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and clots in both lungs. Hurts was first diagnosed with a superficial clot in his calf in London on Oct. 10, then played in the 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. The Eagles later ruled him out of Week 6 and placed him on injured reserve. Reports say he will miss the rest of the season. The team and his agent, Nicole Lynn, said he is clinically stable and expects a full recovery. Feb 9, 2025; New Orleans, LA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) greets Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) following Super Bowl LIX at Ceasars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images “I mean, it’s extremely scary,” Mahomes said. “I mean that it comes from, I guess, a cleat or something like that. I don’t know all the details, but that’s something that happens every single week in the NFL.” Mahomes did not know every detail, but noted that Hurts rarely misses games, which makes a life-threatening clot even harder to process. He added that the news puts football in perspective, since players are human beings with families. Meanwhile, Mahomes was glad doctors found the clots now so Hurts can start treatment, and he hopes the quarterback returns to the field. “So luckily they were able to kind of get it found out now what it actually is and he can get on the medication or whatever it is that he needs to be on and and hopefully he can get back on that field again cuz the NFL’s better when you have great players on it and he’s one of those players.” Hurts will need blood thinners for at least three months, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Mahomes was not the only voice in the story, and questions about the Eagles and their medical decisions are growing. Eagles Face Scrutiny Over Decision to Clear Jalen Hurts for London Game The Eagles are also dealing with pressure from outside the locker room. Their statement said an ultrasound after the team’s flight to London showed a superficial clot, and doctors there concluded Hurts could safely play. He completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown against Jacksonville. On Monday, coach Nick Sirianni declined to explain why the team allowed Hurts to fly home with the clot, according to the Associated Press. Several analysts also questioned whether Hurts should have played on little rest. Tanner McKee has taken over under center. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in a 25-14 loss to the Panthers, which dropped Philadelphia to 2-4 and extended its losing streak to four g

item.title: Former Barcelona defender explains why Flick’s side have the edge over Real Madrid: ‘Not a normal match’
item.description: Former Barcelona defender explains why Flick’s side have the edge over Real Madrid: ‘Not a normal match’ Former Barcelona left-back Sergi Barjuan believes Hansi Flick’s side have the advantage over Real Madrid ahead of Sunday’s El Clasico at Spotify Camp Nou, pointing to their recent form, fitness and tactical structure as reasons to favour the Catalans. However, Barjuan has also warned that the rivalry rarely follows ordinary footballing logic, with Real Madrid arriving after a strong Champions League result and renewed confidence ahead of one of the season’s biggest fixtures. Barjuan also expressed frustration with the growing off-field tension surrounding the Clasico , arguing that discussions in boardrooms and the media have threatened to overshadow the contest itself. Sergi Barjuan believes Barcelona have the edge over Real Madrid Barjuan expects a closely contested match but sees Barcelona as the stronger side based on their current performances. The former defender acknowledged Madrid’s recent progress while suggesting that Flick’s team have shown greater consistency in several important areas. “Barça are in very good form. The statistics speak for themselves. But we’re talking about a Clasico, and a Clasico isn’t a normal match. “Real Madrid are coming off the back of a good win in the Champions League and have been strengthened, but in terms of structure, fitness and results, I see Barça as the better side.” Barjuan criticises off-field Clasico tensions Sergi Barjuan has backed Hansi Flick’s Barcelona. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) Beyond his prediction, Barjuan lamented the extent to which the build-up has focused on disputes away from the pitch. He believes the players should determine the narrative through their performances rather than become secondary figures in a wider exchange between the clubs. “Honestly, it would be great if the talk were solely about football and the spectacle. The players should do their talking on the pitch,” he said. Barjuan subsequently pointed to disagreements over refereeing decisions and accused those involved of being selective about which incidents receive attention. He also referenced Jose Mourinho, suggesting that people involved in football naturally defend their own interests. “Everyone has the right to express their opinion and judge as they see fit. Barça are speaking on the pitch. And that’s where you see the differences between the two teams. “There have been refereeing controversies and they’ve tried to sweep them under the carpet. They don’t see the footage when they don’t want to see it. And vice versa. Barcelona lost to PSG but are still favourites to beat Real Madrid. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) “We know Mourinho well enough; everyone looks out for their own interests. I know him personally and I know what he’s made of,” he added. item.title: 'Not what a captain should be' - the debate around Fernandes' outburst
item.description: Bruno Fernandes' comments after Manchester United's humbling by Como have got fans and pundits talking - but what now for the captain? United's 4-1 Champions League defeat in Italy was the result of a wretched performance and Fernandes questioned boss Michael Carrick's tactics. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence," said the Portugal attacking midfielder on TNT Sports. Asked if Carrick got his tactics wrong, the 32-year-old continued: "That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me." Are these the actions of a captain? Fernandes rounds on Carrick after Man Utd humiliation Man Utd humbling by Como leaves Carrick job in danger Not according to former Liverpool vice-captain Jamie Carragher, working as a summariser, on CBS Sports. "He's reacted like that because he's been embarrassed by the manager [who] brought him off," said the ex-England defender. "And when he talks about pressing, whether it's man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. "He runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard. He's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it." He added: "Watching him throw his arms up every week in a game is an absolute disgrace [and] calling the manager out considering how he's performed this season on the pitch. "[It's an] awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should be." Fernandes' comments come a week after defender Lisandro Martinez made similar headlines following United's previous Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid. The Argentine said he expected more investment in the squad and "more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]". He later apologised. And while Martinez's outburst sparked debate, Fernandes' comments could have even larger repercussions. Carrick, who was under huge pressure already following a terrible start to the season, said in reply: "There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win." United have not won in their past seven games since beating Champions League minnows Sabah. They have just one win in their seven Premier League games this season. 'He should not be saying these things' Not many people have defended Fernandes' public questioning of the tactics. But some do understand his frustrations. Former Leicester and Celtic keeper Kasper Schmeichel, whose dad Peter won the Champions League, five Premier League titles and three FA Cups as a United player, said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "Given last week and what's happened, he probably should not be saying these things because it's only going to add to the problems. "With experience you learn that you need to keep these things in-house.
item.content:encoded: Bruno Fernandes' comments after Manchester United's humbling by Como have got fans and pundits talking - but what now for the captain? United's 4-1 Champions League defeat in Italy was the result of a wretched performance and Fernandes questioned boss Michael Carrick's tactics. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence," said the Portugal attacking midfielder on TNT Sports. Asked if Carrick got his tactics wrong, the 32-year-old continued: "That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me." Are these the actions of a captain? Fernandes rounds on Carrick after Man Utd humiliation Man Utd humbling by Como leaves Carrick job in danger Not according to former Liverpool vice-captain Jamie Carragher, working as a summariser, on CBS Sports. "He's reacted like that because he's been embarrassed by the manager [who] brought him off," said the ex-England defender. "And when he talks about pressing, whether it's man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. "He runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard. He's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it." He added: "Watching him throw his arms up every week in a game is an absolute disgrace [and] calling the manager out considering how he's performed this season on the pitch. "[It's an] awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should be." Fernandes' comments come a week after defender Lisandro Martinez made similar headlines following United's previous Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid. The Argentine said he expected more investment in the squad and "more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]". He later apologised. And while Martinez's outburst sparked debate, Fernandes' comments could have even larger repercussions. Carrick, who was under huge pressure already following a terrible start to the season, said in reply: "There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win." United have not won in their past seven games since beating Champions League minnows Sabah. They have just one win in their seven Premier League games this season. 'He should not be saying these things' Not many people have defended Fernandes' public questioning of the tactics. But some do understand his frustrations. Former Leicester and Celtic keeper Kasper Schmeichel, whose dad Peter won the Champions League, five Premier League titles and three FA Cups as a United player, said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "Given last week and what's happened, he probably should not be saying these things because it's only going to add to the problems. "With experience you learn that you need to keep these things in-house. It's a problem, with everything that happened during the week. "Michael Carrick didn't need this, the club didn't need this. It's exposing all of the issues that are at Manchester United. "It's very plain to see that there are loads of issues but you need to be fixing them, you need to be having meetings within the club, which I'm sure that they are, but it's obviously not resolved. It's just translating on to the pitch." The issue that most pundits have is not that Fernandes has these opinions - but that he has let the world know them. Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock, speaking on BBC Match of the Day, said: "I think there will be ex-players now from Manchester United saying, 'why are you letting this get out, this should be a collective in the changing room where we come together'. "Whether you like the manager or not, you've got to come together and say 'OK how do we correct this?' "Senior players go to the manager and say 'listen we didn't agree with the tactics, we didn't think we got it right, how do we go about this, how do we move forward', because you start airing it in public and it doesn't end well for anyone." Former Chelsea midfielder Joe Cole on TNT Sports called it "sacrilege". "I've played for managers where I don't agree with the tactics but you might say that to your mate or to your wife. You don't come out as captain of the club and question the manager," he said. What do the fans think? Andy Mitten, editor of United We Stand, told BBC 5 Live Breakfast that Fernandes has "thrown his coach under the bus". "It's a terrible look," he continued. "And Manchester United fans are divided as to whether he should or should not do that. Last week, Martinez was also critical. A lot of Manchester United fans agreed with him. "Again, there's mitigation, he wants a new contract. That's because he's not been playing enough, because he's been injured. And injuries are a real problem for Manchester United. There's no recognised centre-forward. So it is a really difficult time for United." Former United midfielder Carrick, who took over in January initially as caretaker manager, seemed to blank his players at full-time before heading over to the United fans. "I don't blame him for ignoring the players," said Mitten. "He went to the fans and he held his hands up and he said, 'I'm sorry'. "You can tell he's hurting. He's a Manchester United fan himself. He was a season ticket holder only a year ago before he took the job. I think he's trying his best, but it's just not working at the moment. Manchester United are really, really struggling." What now for Fernandes? Bruno Fernandes has been United's captain for three years [Getty Images] Fernandes has been Manchester United's one consistent outstanding player since a £47m move from Sporting in January 2020, when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was the manager. He has scored 111 goals and made 106 assists in 338 games for the club in all competitions. Former manager Erik ten Hag made him the skipper in the summer of 2023 after taking the armband off Harry Maguire, whose place in the team was far from certain. But this is not the first time his body language, attitude and behaviour as captain has been criticised. He was called a "disgrace" and "embarrassing" by United legends Gary Neville and Roy Keane after the 7-0 loss to Liverpool in 2023, while Chris Sutton said he should never captain the club again. However, last season Fernandes was named the Premier League's player of the year after a record 21 assists in a season. "That award was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager," said Carragher. "He wouldn't have got that award without Michael Carrick, because Michael Carrick put him back in his rightful position and he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. "But in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all." Fernandes has made headlines with his comments before. In August 2025 he said the club needed to make more signings. That December he was asked about the fact United had been willing to sell him to Al-Hilal and told Canal 11: "From the club I felt it was, 'If you go it's not so bad for us'. It hurts me a bit. "More than hurting me, it makes me sad. I'm a player that no-one can criticise, I'm always available, I always give my best. "I could have left in this transfer window, I would have earned much more money. "I would have won many trophies this season, but I decided not to go, not only for family reasons but because I genuinely love the club." But now the narrative might change entirely after his latest comments. Many will be wondering whether he should even start in Sunday's game against Bournemouth. Martinez did keep his place, after apologising, at Leeds last Sunday. But as United fan Mitten says: ''There was mitigation with Martinez because he wants a new contract. Fernandes is captain." There has been no word from the

item.title: Raptors send frightening early message with 43-point destruction of Bulls
item.description: Raptors send frightening early message with 43-point destruction of Bulls originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Raptors could hardly have imagined a more convincing beginning to the 2026-27 NBA season. Toronto overwhelmed the Chicago Bulls 135-92 on Wednesday night, delivering a 43-point victory that immediately generated excitement about the team's potential. The Raptors controlled the game with aggressive defense, perimeter shooting and contributions from several key players. Scottie Barnes finished with 23 points, six rebounds and five assists. Kawhi Leonard also scored 23 points, adding six assists and four steals in his first regular-season appearance since returning to Toronto. The win provided an encouraging opening statement for a franchise hoping to become a serious factor in the Eastern Conference. It also exposed significant problems for Chicago. Kawhi Leonard's return provides early excitement Leonard's return to the Raptors was one of the NBA's most intriguing offseason developments. The veteran forward previously helped Toronto win the 2019 NBA championship, earning Finals MVP honors during that historic run. His return gives the Raptors another experienced player capable of contributing on both ends of the floor. "I'm just going to play hard and try to have fun out there, and try to make the city proud." Kawhi (23 PTS, 6 REB, 4 STL) on his Raptors return 👏 https://t.co/YbRECRgJ0q — NBA (@NBA) October 22, 2026 Wednesday's performance was not perfect. Leonard made five of his 17 field-goal attempts, demonstrating that his offensive efficiency still has room for improvement. However, he found other ways to influence the game. His six assists helped Toronto maintain offensive movement, while his four steals contributed to a dominant defensive performance. Barnes also delivered an encouraging effort. The versatile forward made eight of 19 shots and showed the scoring ability that could become even more important with Leonard alongside him. Together, the two provide Toronto with an intriguing combination of size, playmaking and defensive versatility. Their opening game offered few encouraging signs. Josh Giddey endured a particularly difficult evening, scoring just two points on 1-of-10 shooting. RJ Barrett helped set the defensive tone for Toronto, making life difficult for Chicago's primary ballhandler. The Bulls also struggled without center Nic Claxton, leaving them vulnerable around the basket. Toronto took advantage of those problems while building a commanding lead. By the final minutes, the outcome was no longer in doubt. The Raptors were able to finish the game comfortably as their home crowd celebrated an impressive opening

item.title: Joel Klatt reveals Big Ten-SEC scheduling plan for when playoff increases to 24 teams
item.description: A 24-team College Football Playoff has has been all but confirmed as starting as soon as next season, and there’s been no shortage of criticism for what feels like a largely unnecessary move. TT Big Ten and SEC, the primary driving force behind the College Football Playoff expansion push, have more plans in the works for when the expansion is finally ratified, per Fox’s Joel Klatt. “There are scheduling agreements that are in place once this thing expands officially,” Klatt told KTCK-FM 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas on Wednesday, per Football Scoop. “The next thing that will happen almost immediately is we’re going to get scheduling agreements between the SEC and the Big Ten; top-end matchups, mid-tier matchups, low-end matchups — and we’re going to be expanding the valuable matchups in the non-conference, far surpassing what we have now.” Big Ten commissioner Tony Petititi guaranteed earlier this month that with playoff expansion the conference would commit to a minimum of 10 Power 4 games. “We need to play more good games. I think we’ve been really clear about that. We think that the season can start way better than it does. We’re committed to that. If we get to a 24-team Playoff, you are going to see many more competitive games scheduled,” he said. However, as many grand plans as the Big Ten and SEC may have in the works, there will undoubtedly also be plenty of unintended consequences, even for the sport’s two premier conferences, and ESPN’s Dan Wetzel has already predicted a massive one that may lead each to regret pushing for the expansion. “Notre Dame now has the best situation in all of football – almost 100 percent guarantee to make the playoff, freedom to schedule as it wishes, maximization of its own media value,” he wrote on X. “To use the Big Ten as an example, why wouldn’t Ohio State, Michigan and Penn State follow? If you can, be independent. That’s the future,” he continued. “The 18-team Big Ten is bloated, distant, and winning it carries little intrinsic or competitive value for the biggest brands. “Those three schools can create a scheduling agreement that would increase their media revenue 2-3x and give the same control over everything. No sharing money. No forced TV times. Eight or even nine home games. Select your own schedule. Staying in the Big Ten now makes little and perhaps no economic sense.” College football will change substantially once playoff expansion officially passes. Only time will tell exactly what all of that change looks like. The post Joel Klatt reveals Big Ten-SEC scheduling plan for when playoff increases to 24 teams appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: The Timberwolves Just Gave Their Critics Something to Explain
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Timberwolves were supposed to have a problem with teams built like the Miami Heat. After trading Julius Randle and Naz Reid, Minnesota entered the season with understandable questions about its size, rebounding and ability to withstand physical opponents. A faster offense sounded exciting. Finding enough muscle around Rudy Gobert looked considerably less certain. Then the Wolves opened against Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo — and won the rebounding battle by 14. Anthony Edwards’ 45 points will dominate the conversation after Minnesota’s 131–106 victory Wednesday night. LaMelo Ball’s debut supplied plenty of highlights, too. But the most encouraging numbers for anyone worried about this roster might be found elsewhere in the box score . Minnesota finished with 52 rebounds to Miami’s 38. The offensive-rebounding margin was even more striking: 17–4. One game cannot settle a season-long concern. It can, however, complicate the assumption that the new Wolves will be easy to push around. The Timberwolves had been preparing for this test Oct 8, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) dribbles the basketball against the New Orleans Pelicans during the first quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Miami offered an immediate examination of Minnesota’s new identity. Antetokounmpo and Adebayo can attack with size, speed and power, forcing defenders to absorb contact while remaining disciplined. The Wolves knew what was coming. According to Edwards, they had spent much of the offseason preparing each other for precisely that kind of challenge. “If you see how we’ve been playing against each other for the past two months, then you’ll know we’re ready for physical teams,” Edwards said in his postgame interview . “We’ve been going at each other for the last two months. So it felt good to go put it on somebody else.” Ball offered a specific example of that daily pressure, pointing to Ayo Dosunmu’s willingness to defend the length of the floor. “With Ayo picking up full court every day,” Ball said, describing the team’s preparation in his postgame presser . “You’ve got a lot of players on the team just going at each other, for real.” That is useful context for a group whose offseason has often been discussed in terms of pace, shooting and personality. The players describe a preparation process that also demanded consistent effort against one another. Finch saw another benefit from those sessions: players arrived ready to work. “I’ve never been around a team that we didn’t have to worry about getting anyone in shape this preseason,” he noted after the game. Conditioning alone will not win a rebounding battle. It does help a team sustain the movement, contact and repeated efforts required to compete. Rudy Gobert had help on the glass Credit: Matt Krohn-USA TODAY Sports Gobert did his part, collecting 15 rebounds, including five on offense. Yet Minnesota

Antetokounmpo and Adebayo can attack with size, speed and power, forcing defenders to absorb contact while remaining disciplined. The Wolves knew what was coming. According to Edwards, they had spent much of the offseason preparing each other for precisely that kind of challenge. “If you see how we’ve been playing against each other for the past two months, then you’ll know we’re ready for physical teams,” Edwards said in his postgame interview . “We’ve been going at each other for the last two months. So it felt good to go put it on somebody else.” Ball offered a specific example of that daily pressure, pointing to Ayo Dosunmu’s willingness to defend the length of the floor. “With Ayo picking up full court every day,” Ball said, describing the team’s preparation in his postgame presser . “You’ve got a lot of players on the team just going at each other, for real.” That is useful context for a group whose offseason has often been discussed in terms of pace, shooting and personality. The players describe a preparation process that also demanded consistent effort against one another. Finch saw another benefit from those sessions: players arrived ready to work. “I’ve never been around a team that we didn’t have to worry about getting anyone in shape this preseason,” he noted after the game. Conditioning alone will not win a rebounding battle. It does help a team sustain the movement, contact and repeated efforts required to compete. Rudy Gobert had help on the glass Credit: Matt Krohn-USA TODAY Sports Gobert did his part, collecting 15 rebounds, including five on offense. Yet Minnesota’s advantage extended beyond its starting center. Edwards grabbed 10 rebounds. Jaden McDaniels added eight. Joan Beringer collected six in fewer than 14 minutes, and Dosunmu contributed five, including three offensive boards. That distribution matters for a roster relying on more athleticism around Gobert. If the Wolves are going to hold up against bigger opponents, their guards and wings have to participate in finishing possessions. Wednesday provided a good example of what that can look like. Minnesota repeatedly created another opportunity after a miss while allowing Miami only four offensive rebounds. There is a distinction between playing smaller and accepting that the opponent will control the glass. The Wolves showed they can challenge that outcome through collective involvement. McDaniels described a similar mindset toward contact. “Just knowing that teams are going to try to be physical with us and then just embracing the physicality,” he added in the locker room. He also emphasized maintaining Minnesota’s own game while responding to the opponent. The Wolves do not need to abandon their faster approach every time a bigger team appears on the schedule. They need to support it with enough resistance and rebounding to keep playing it. Jonathan Kuminga gave Minnesota an important option Kuminga’s work against Antetokounmpo was another encouraging development. Finch singled him out afterward, praising his willingness to contest catches, meet Antetokounmpo early and keep applying his body throughout possessions. Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-USA TODAY Sports “He just wasn’t afraid to put his body on him continually,” Finch said when explaining the matchup. Antetokounmpo still scored 35 points on 13-of-19 shooting. Minnesota did not erase his influence, and Kuminga was clear that stopping everything was never a realistic expectation. His explanation was straightforward: keep making the assignment difficult. “I won’t give up because we’re trying to win these games,” Kuminga said in his postgame interview . “We’re trying to establish something over here.” That persistence gives Finch something valuable as he works through his rotation. Minnesota needs players willing to accept demanding assignments without allowing an opponent’s success to dictate their effort on the next possession. The opener also left questions. The reserve frontcourt had difficult stretches, and Gobert cannot be expected to solve every matchup. Opponents will study the Wolves, test their depth and force adjustments. But Minnesota’s first answer deserves attention. Against a powerful Miami frontcourt, the Wolves competed through contact, dominated the offensive glass and received rebounding contributions throughout the rotation. The concerns about their size were reasonable. After Wednesday, treating physicality as an automatic weakness looks considerably less convincing. Related Headlines Anthony Edwards Has One Rule for Anyone Talking Trash Minnesota Timberwolves Fans Should Be Furious Habs Daily: Beck And Reinbacher, Indiscipline Issues, Zharovsky Highlight Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: “Emotional To See” – Andre Agassi Reveals Why Alexander Zverev’s 2026 Success Despite Criticism Means So Much to Him
item.description: Jun 8, 2025; Paris, FR; Andre Agassi at the trophy presentation for the Carlos Alcaraz of Spain and Jannik Sinner of Italy men’s singles final match on day 15 at Roland Garros Stadium. © Susan Mullane-Imagn Images Tennis legend Andre Agassi recently expressed admiration for Alexander Zverev and explained why the German player’s 2026 feats matter. Zverev has had a breakthrough season, winning his first two career major titles at the French Open and the US Open. He saw off Flavio Cobolli 6–1, 4–6, 6–4, 6–7, 6–1 to clinch his first Major title at Roland Garros. He defeated the home favorite Ben Shelton 6–3, 7–6(2), 5–7, 6–2 on the Arthur Ashe Stadium to lift the US Open trophy. Zverev made a semifinal run at the Australian Open before being seen off by Carlos Alcaraz. He also reached the final at Wimbledon, where Jannik Sinner beat him 7–6(9), 6–7(2), 3–6, 4–6. Although Zverev faced criticism for winning titles in the absence of Alcaraz and Sinner, who were absent due to injuries or early exits, Andre Agassi appreciated the German tennis player. When asked about his favorite tennis moment of 2026 in an interview with Tennis Channel, the former World No. 1 highlighted Zverev’s feat, saying it was emotional to see his hard work finally pay off. “Oh God, you guys really put me on the spot. The story of this was Sascha getting over the line for his first Slam. That was his… that was, you know, emotional to see. Sascha is one of the hardest workers on the Tour and having that rewarded with finally achieving, you can’t help but feel good about it. Great to see Carlitos back, and I hope Sinner is using his time wisely because, you know, those two guys are so good for the game. So let’s hope for even better things in 2027.” Zverev’s French Open win made him the first German man to win a Grand Slam singles title in 30 years, since Boris Becker at the 1996 Australian Open. Andy Roddick reacts to Andre Agassi’s playful take on Alexander Zverev following the Laver Cup During the post-match speech at the 2026 Laver Cup, Andre Agassi took a light-hearted jab at Alexander Zverev, highlighting the latter’s first two career Grand Slam wins. “Congratulations, Sascha, on a crazy year,” Agassi said. “Seeing you win [a Grand Slam] for the first time, I know how important that was to you, and it was important to me too, because I could start listening to your press conferences again. You weren’t like, ‘Waah, why do I always lose? Why am I the third best in the world? I suck’. But then you win, and it’s like, ‘I’m only a one-time Slam champion; I’ve got to do it again.” Roddick praised Agassi’s ability to switch quickly from joking to expressing appreciation and highlighted his team’s love for him. “Andre [Agassi] has an unbelievable ability to shift gears very, very quickly. He can go from kind of roasting Zverev to having a very heartfelt moment to his team. His team loves playing for him; by the way, there is no doubt about it,” said Roddick. Team Europe, including Zve

item.title: ‘Pure arrogance’: anger in Finland as Google illegally fells 250,000 trees for datacentre
item.description: Company ordered to stop work at two sites in country, which has found itself at forefront of tech firms’ latest push Behind a wire fence lies a vast gaping wound of earth. Before Google’s arrival a few months ago, an estimated quarter of a million trees occupied the 330 hectares (815 acres) of forest near the town of Muhos in rural northern Finland. Now they are all gone. After the tech company illegally stripped the entire area to build a datacentre – taking even the top soil with it – all that remains is a vast expanse of mud indented with the trail marks of machinery, puddles and mounds of earth, roots and branches. Residents say that brown water flowing off the site is going into a stream that feeds the Oulujoki River. Continue reading...

item.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
item.description: Austrian’s tactics need adapting to but Forest are in the bottom three and their owner is not the patient type Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground: it is not the dream start they were aiming for. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. Continue reading...

item.title: Marc Marquez retirement predicted if he wins tenth MotoGP world title
item.description: Marc Marquez could be just five races from retirement. That’s according to MotoGP race winner Marco Melandri, who thinks a tenth championship would be enough for the legend to call it quits. Marquez regularly spoke about his time in the sport coming to an end at the start of the season amid more injury troubles that culminated in a teary Le Mans exit and double surgery. Since then, he’s performed yet another remarkable title turnaround and is considered by most as the 2026 championship favourite. During that time there were two other key developments - Marquez signed a new contract, and got a new teammate for 2027 in the shape of Pedro Acosta . According to Melandri, that latter factor could play a huge part in what happens this winter. Pedro Acosta emerges as key factor in Marquez retirement prediction The five-time MotoGP race winner said: "For me, if Marquez wins his tenth World Championship, he could retire. "Nobody can know for sure. But Ducati needs a plan B, which it doesn't have right now. “Marquez knows that Acosta, his future teammate, can beat him. He's the first teammate who could achieve that, and it could happen. “Furthermore, he's following the political and regulatory changes brought about by Liberty Media, with their events and the new format. There are many factors in favour of him retiring if he wins tenth time.” Marquez signed a two-year extension with Ducati for 2027 and 2028, but it later emerged that it was a ‘1+1 deal’ meaning 2028 is an option both parties would speak about at the end of next season. Many think Acosta could push Marquez to retire (Credit: Red Bull Content Pool) Many think Acosta could push Marquez to retire (Credit: Red Bull Content Pool) Marquez's Ducati contract may not guarantee his long-term future Next year brings about a string of regulation changes, including smaller engines, less aerodynamics and Pirelli tyres. It also sees a record 22 events and the introduction of a second qualifying session, something Marquez has publicly criticised . He’s also spoken out against Liberty Media bringing in fines for riders who fail to show up for promotional events. Adding his voice to the complaints about the new rules, Marquez claimed they will bring forward the end of his career. Recently speaking about his future, the 33-year-old also suggested he could retire in the next few years. What Marquez has said about leaving MotoGP In an interview with MotoGP, he commented: "I'm here and competing because, for now, I haven't thrown in the towel mentally. "I've already achieved a lot, but I still feel competitive. And I know that, if I want to, I can remain competitive for a few more years. "But we're not in a sport like football or tennis, where you give 100 per cent, although the risk is much lower. "So, there are many factors to consider in MotoGP before retiring. He commented: "I can't compare him to Agostini because he has the best track record and he did things that are impossible now, like winning two titles at the same time. “But Marquez spent four years away, and now you see him fighting for his tenth... item.title: Former WWE stars sign new 5-year AEW deal
item.description: Former WWE stars sign new 5-year AEW deal appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Earlier this year at AEW All In 2026, former WWE Superstars Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods made their All Elite Wrestling debut . Going with Kofi and Austin Creed, the duo made their debut in the Trios title match. Paired with Swerve Strickland, the three of them won the AEW Trios Championship before losing it to Adam Page, Bandido, and Brody King at AEW WrestleDream 2026. Now, Fightful Select has reported a major update on New Level’s [Kofi & Austin Creed] AEW contract. “New Level signed five-year AEW contracts,” Fightful Select said. According to the report, Kofi and Creed were pitched to join AEW and work with Strickland. It was also added that Strickland played a major role in bridging the relationship between the duo and AEW, as Tony Khan was hesitant to speak with them before their WWE contract was over. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Long before joining AEW as New Level, Creed and Kofi were known as The New Day in WWE. While popular babyface wrestlers almost throughout their careers, Kofi and Woods turned heel toward the final run of their careers. AEW’s New Level talk about their WWE salary paycut Just days after making their AEW debut, Kofi and Creed of The New Level appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show, where they opened up in detail about their alleged WWE pay cut. “Compensation was definitely a big part, but more so, we wanted to work. We wanted to go out there and showcase our skills and showcase our talents. We wanted to do what we love. We love going out there and messing with fans, threatening to ground kids, and really garner reactions to people, and send them home with incredible memories they’ll never forget. I don’t know exactly what’s out there. I will say, it was more than 50 percent, which a lot of people don’t know,” Kofi said.

item.title: Walker Kessler equals Wilt Chamberlain in historic Lakers 56-year feat vs. Warriors
item.description: Walker Kessler equals Wilt Chamberlain in historic Lakers 56-year feat vs. Warriors originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Panacea acquisitions are rare in the NBA. Teams sign many players to fill specific gaps, but they have their own weaknesses that eventually get exposed. Walker Kessler seems like a rare panacea signing for the Los Angeles Lakers . He helped Luka Doncic and JJ Redick get an opening night 127-105 win over the Golden State Warriors . More than that, he was also the best big man on the floor. It was proven when he matched an insane record by Wilt Chamberlain. Kessler gets historic NBA feat achieved by Chamberlain in Lakers vs. Warriors The Lakers had a lot of holes to fix during the NBA offseason. Coach JJ Redick had to build schemes around Luka Doncic without LeBron James on the roster. They also lost big men like Jaxson Hayes and Deandre Ayton. So the natural solution was to find someone who could fill all those holes at once. This is where Walker Kessler comes in. On paper, he is the perfect player to slot alongside Doncic and complement Coach Redick's schemes. When the Lakers faced the Warriors, it was time to put those skills and ideas into practice. Kessler delivered. Coach Redick gave him 30 minutes to anchor the Lakers' defense and serve as the perfect big man to help Doncic. How great was his Lakers debut? Kessler finished with 26 points on 100% from the field. He also got an assist. Defensively, Coach Redick saw him grab nine rebounds while snagging two blocks. Kessler's 100% from the field wasn't just a great Lakers debut; it also matched a record only Wilt Chamberlain came close to. The new Lakers big man went 12-for-12 from the field. Only Chamberlain finished with more in his 14-for-14 game on March 11, 1969, against the Detroit Pistons , via ESPN Insights. I think that’s why he wanted to be a Laker. And why he wanted to be here was because of the fact that there are stakes every single night when you wear a Lakers uniform. We’ve had a number of conversations. We had a long conversation the other day about it. I think the awareness is there; how you navigate that early on and how you navigate that in your first year, there’s no way to predict that because you’ve never dealt with it before. By the end, Coach Redick and the Lakers seem to have found the perfect running mate for Doncic. The Lakers superstar also scored 28 points of his own, and it all got easier with Kessler manning the paint. All of this helped the Lakers get their first win of the season. item.title: Meet Nkechi Okenwa, the Engineer Helping More Nigerian Women Break Into Renewable Energy
item.description: Tokunbo Adegoju during an interview with bird story agency at the Automedics workshop in Illepeju, Lagos, July 10, 2026. Photo: Dorcas Bello, bird story agency Nkechi Okenwa walked into her office, moving instinctively toward the window and pulled the blinds open. Outside, the city was already in motion: cars weaving through traffic, traders arranging their stalls, generators humming faintly in the distance. She paused for a moment and smiled quietly to herself. For Nkechi, energy had never simply been about electricity. It was about movement, opportunity, and the power to transform lives. Long before she stepped into a university lecture hall, Nkechi said, she had been fascinated by the way a single switch could completely change the atmosphere of a home. Growing up in Nigeria, she watched how electricity brought light into dark rooms and how access to power allowed communities and businesses to function. “As a teenager choosing the course of study, I had to take on electrical electronics engineering as a course,” she recalls. “Though I knew it was a male-dominated call, because I never saw any female studying that course… that’s actually how this whole journey started.” When she finally entered university, the reality of that gender gap became impossible to ignore. In a lecture hall of more than 220 engineering students, only 12 were women — barely five percent of the class. The imbalance was intimidating, but it also planted the seed for a bigger mission. item.content:encoded: Tokunbo Adegoju during an interview with bird story agency at the Automedics workshop in Illepeju, Lagos, July 10, 2026. Photo: Dorcas Bello, bird story agency Nkechi Okenwa walked into her office, moving instinctively toward the window and pulled the blinds open. Outside, the city was already in motion: cars weaving through traffic, traders arranging their stalls, generators humming faintly in the distance. She paused for a moment and smiled quietly to herself. For Nkechi, energy had never simply been about electricity. It was about movement, opportunity, and the power to transform lives. Long before she stepped into a university lecture hall, Nkechi said, she had been fascinated by the way a single switch could completely change the atmosphere of a home. Growing up in Nigeria, she watched how electricity brought light into dark rooms and how access to power allowed communities and businesses to function. “As a teenager choosing the course of study, I had to take on electrical electronics engineering as a course,” she recalls. “Though I knew it was a male-dominated call, because I never saw any female studying that course… that’s actually how this whole journey started.” When she finally entered university, the reality of that gender gap became impossible to ignore. In a lecture hall of more than 220 engineering students, only 12 were women — barely five percent of the class. The imbalance was intimidating, but it also planted the seed for a bigger mission. Tokunbo Adegoju during her radio show at the Eko FM in LTV premises 1, lateef Jakande way , Agidingbi ikeja, Lagos, July 9, 2026. Photo: Dorcas Bello, bird story agency “I said there has to be a way to, you know, get women inclusive.” “I understand the challenges that come with a female being in this male-dominated industry, but when I look at myself and I can remember how I was able to go through, the challenges, my persistence, and all of that, I told myself it’s possible that so many other women too have aspirations to make a difference in their world and can also do this, so it made me start thinking of starting this organisation.” Years later, that determination evolved into two major ventures. Today, Nkechi serves as the CEO of Energy Excell Systems and Solutions and is also the founder of the Women in Energy and Economic Sustainability Initiative (WEESI), which is dedicated to integrating women into every level of the renewable energy sector. Tokunbo Adegoju repairing a car at the Automedics workshop in Illepeju, Lagos, July 10, 2026. Photo: Dorcas Bello, bird story agency Her professional journey did not begin with entrepreneurship. After graduating, she started as a technical staff member at an IT company where she worked with power systems and tools like AutoCAD. Through workshops, conferences, and industry engagements, she became increasingly exposed to the renewable energy sector at a time when Nigeria was slowly beginning to embrace alternative energy solutions. She later transitioned into a sales executive role before eventually building her own solar installation company. Established in 2013, Energy Excell Systems and Solutions Limited operates as an indigenous Nigerian renewable energy social enterprise and Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) company. But beyond simply installing solar panels, the company focused heavily on what Nkechi describes as “productive use” energy. The company provided homes, small businesses, and farming communities with energy-efficient appliances such as solar-powered rice mills, cassava graters, and grinders: tools capable of directly improving livelihoods and local economies. Tokunbo Adegoju and fellow mechanics discussing with each other at the Automedics workshop in Illepeju, Lagos, July 10, 2026. Photo: Dorcas Bello, bird story agency As her business expanded, Nkechi noticed another problem that extended far beyond electricity access. Women remained largely absent from conversations around energy solutions, despite being among the most affected by energy poverty within communities. “I looked at women, and I found that most challenges in the community that we face, we face them as men and women, but I find that women sometimes are not really included in solving these challenges, so I told myself I have to find a way to get women to across all levels.” That realisation led to the creation of WEESI in 2020. The initiative was designed to create pathways for women and girls across the energy value chain, from rural communities at the bottom of the energy pyramid to leadership spaces within the sector. The organisation strategically tailored its programs across different age groups. For girls and young women between the ages of 12 and 26, WEESI organised STEM essay competitions, mentorship programmes, and scholarship opportunities aimed at nurturing early interest in renewable energy and engineering. Tokunbo Adegoju and fellow mechanics discussing with each other at the Automedics workshop in Illepeju, Lagos, July 10, 2026. Photo: Dorcas Bello, bird story agency At the grassroots level, the initiative focused heavily on economic empowerment. Rural women, community entrepreneurs, and internally displaced persons (IDPs) received technical training in solar photovoltaic installation and maintenance while also learning sustainable clean cooking practices. “We have carried out programs and trainings with women in the rural areas, ranging from telling them how to turn the waste in the community into energy, like making and manufacturing charcoal briquettes with the waste in the community. For example, a woman that threshes rice and has a heap of rice husk doesn’t even know what to do with it. Now, can decarbonise this rice husk into charcoal and make briquettes with them, and make profitable money from it?” For many women, the impact of WEESI became life-changing. Tokunbo Adegoju and fellow mechanics discussing with each other at the Automedics workshop in Illepeju, Lagos, July 10, 2026. Photo: Dorcas Bello, bird story agency Among them was Anita Manuel , an entrepreneur and contractor working with an oil and gas firm. Anita first encountered WEESI during its launch and immediately felt drawn to the organisation’s mission. “What drew me to the initiative is that their objectives aligned with my values and goals too, and I just wanted to expand my business,” Manuel said. Through the training, Manuel learned practical skills in solar panel installation, energy auditing, and technical troubleshooting. More importantly, she began to see how her background in project management and civil works could fit into the renewable energy sector. One moment, however, remained unforgettable. The first time she participated in a successful solar installation that powered an entire building and activated a freezer became a defining experience. For Manuel, it was proof that the technical knowledge she had gained was not theoretical; it was transformative. Mechanics at the Automedics workshop repairing a car in Illepeju, Lagos, July 10, 2026. Photo: Dorcas Bello, bird story agency For Nkechi, her growing influence in the renewable energy space was a quieter battle many women in STEM continue to face: self-doubt and institutional bias. Even after earning her engineering degree, she often questioned whether people would truly trust her expertise in such a male-dominated field. “My fears were, are you sure that I’m going to do it right? Are you sure people are going to listen to me because I’m a woman?” Those fears were reinforced repeatedly in professional spaces. Clients frequently walked into her office searching for a male engineer, assuming she could not possibly hold the technical expertise herself. Tokunbo Adegoju engaging with new students on their first day at the Automedics workshop in Illepeju, Lagos, July 10, 2026. item.title: Milwaukee Bucks’ Myles Turner sends clear message to the team after first loss vs. Washington Wizards
item.description: Myles Turner doubled down on Taylor Jenkins’ take about the Milwaukee Bucks’ 128-116 road loss to the Washington Wizards on Wednesday, saying the game was a huge learning experience for the team, which is currently in its rebuilding phase. Turner felt the Milwaukee Bucks missed a golden opportunity to notch their first win of the 2026-27 campaign, especially since they led most of the game. Milwaukee built a 96-90 lead early in the fourth quarter before Washington went on a 21-2 run to shift the momentum. What Myles Turner said about the Milwaukee Bucks’ opener vs. Washington Wizards Oct 21, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Washington Wizards guard Trae Young (3) shoots the ball as Milwaukee Bucks center Myles Turner (3) defends in the first half at Capital One Arena. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Myles Turner is embracing his veteran leadership role with the Milwaukee Bucks. After Wednesday’s loss, he urged his teammates to continue developing good habits that will eventually translate to on-court success. “My message to the team after the game was, fellas, from the first preseason game to where we’re at now, we’ve gotten a lot better,” Turner said. “And one of the things I hate that people say, but it’s true, is that ‘It’s a long season.’ Yeah, it’s the first game, but if you keep looking at it like, ‘ Hey, it’s a long season, you feel like, ‘OK, we’ll get there eventually.’ That’s not really our mindset. Obviously, we’re building and want to get better every single night, but I think we took a step in the right direction tonight.” Tyler Herro sticks to the positives in the Milwaukee Bucks’ performance Tyler Herro led the Milwaukee Bucks with 24 points, nine assists, and four three-pointers on 9-for-21 shooting in his official debut for his hometown team. After the game, the one-time All-Star lauded the team’s willingness to share the rock, as they had 28 assists on 41 field goals made. “I thought we moved the ball well at times. It got a little sticky, I think, when they went on a run a little bit… I think when we were under control and getting the ball to where it needs to go, and then guys were just playing the right way and making the right decisions, we got the shots we wanted,” Herro said. item.title: Beyond Price Predictions: Exploring Binarium’s Trading Tools and Features
item.description: Ask a beginner what trading is, and the answer is usually “guessing whether a price will go up or down.” But the click that opens a trade is the shortest part of the process. What shapes your results is everything around it: how you practise, how you read the market, where your ideas come from and how you manage risk. That is why a platform’s tools matter more than its buttons. Binarium is an online trading platform that has been operating since 2012. It is available in a browser and as an Android or iOS app, and offers up to 129 assets depending on the account type. The platform supports naira accounts and local payment methods for Nigerian users. Around the trade ticket sits a full set of learning and analysis tools: a demo account, a TradingView chart, an economic calendar, a Trading Room with ideas from experienced traders. This guide explains what each tool does, why it is useful and where its limits are. 1. The Binarium demo account: practise with a purpose New users receive a demo account with ₦10,000,000 in virtual funds. You can switch between demo and real accounts at any time by clicking your balance in the terminal. Demo funds cannot be withdrawn. You can explore the platform’s features through a Binarium demo account before considering real-money trading. Alt: Binarium trading platform A trade is simple in structure: choose an asset, an expiry time and an amount, then decide whether the price will be higher or lower at expiry. If the asset shows a 90% payout and you stake ₦10,000, a correct prediction returns your stake plus ₦9,000, while a wrong one costs the full ₦10,000. Payouts vary by asset. Instead of clicking around, give the demo a job: Test one idea repeatedly, such as one indicator on one timeframe, and see how it behaves over many trades. Review the History section afterwards and look for patterns in your own decisions. Notice how you react after a loss. That is the habit worth fixing before real money is involved. Alt: trading history Binarium A demo cannot reproduce the emotions of live trading, so a good result there does not prove you are ready. 2. Charts and analysis tools: reading before reacting The chart is the center of the terminal. It integrates with the Trading view chart, a charting tool many traders around the world already know. Learn its lines first. A horizontal line follows the current price, a dotted vertical line marks the last moment you can open a trade, and a second vertical line marks expiry, when the result is decided. The panel on the right shows the payout percentage and the amount you would receive on a correct prediction, so you can see what is at stake before you click. Alt: Binarium chart The terminal’s chart can be switched between area, candlestick, bar and line views. Candle size ranges from 5 seconds to 6 hours, and the chart period from 1 minute to 1 day. A line chart shows the overall direction, while candlesticks add the open, high, low and close of each period. Alt: candle size Binari
item.dc:creator: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
item.content:encoded: Ask a beginner what trading is, and the answer is usually “guessing whether a price will go up or down.” But the click that opens a trade is the shortest part of the process. What shapes your results is everything around it: how you practise, how you read the market, where your ideas come from and how you manage risk. That is why a platform’s tools matter more than its buttons. Binarium is an online trading platform that has been operating since 2012. It is available in a browser and as an Android or iOS app, and offers up to 129 assets depending on the account type. The platform supports naira accounts and local payment methods for Nigerian users. Around the trade ticket sits a full set of learning and analysis tools: a demo account, a TradingView chart, an economic calendar, a Trading Room with ideas from experienced traders. This guide explains what each tool does, why it is useful and where its limits are. 1. The Binarium demo account: practise with a purpose New users receive a demo account with ₦10,000,000 in virtual funds. You can switch between demo and real accounts at any time by clicking your balance in the terminal. Demo funds cannot be withdrawn. You can explore the platform’s features through a Binarium demo account before considering real-money trading. Alt: Binarium trading platform A trade is simple in structure: choose an asset, an expiry time and an amount, then decide whether the price will be higher or lower at expiry. If the asset shows a 90% payout and you stake ₦10,000, a correct prediction returns your stake plus ₦9,000, while a wrong one costs the full ₦10,000. Payouts vary by asset. Instead of clicking around, give the demo a job: Test one idea repeatedly, such as one indicator on one timeframe, and see how it behaves over many trades. Review the History section afterwards and look for patterns in your own decisions. Notice how you react after a loss. That is the habit worth fixing before real money is involved. Alt: trading history Binarium A demo cannot reproduce the emotions of live trading, so a good result there does not prove you are ready. 2. Charts and analysis tools: reading before reacting The chart is the center of the terminal. It integrates with the Trading view chart, a charting tool many traders around the world already know. Learn its lines first. A horizontal line follows the current price, a dotted vertical line marks the last moment you can open a trade, and a second vertical line marks expiry, when the result is decided. The panel on the right shows the payout percentage and the amount you would receive on a correct prediction, so you can see what is at stake before you click. Alt: Binarium chart The terminal’s chart can be switched between area, candlestick, bar and line views. Candle size ranges from 5 seconds to 6 hours, and the chart period from 1 minute to 1 day. A line chart shows the overall direction, while candlesticks add the open, high, low and close of each period. Alt: candle size Binarium website The standard chart includes popular indicators and drawing tools: SMA (simple moving average) smooths price data so the underlying trend is easier to see. Bollinger Bands show how stretched the price is compared with its recent range. Drawing tools such as segments and curves let you mark support, resistance and channels directly on the chart. Alt: indicators Binarium Two lesser-known features help too. On the desktop you can view up to four charts in one window, which makes it easier to compare assets. And the trader sentiment scale shows what share of current trades on an asset expect the price to rise and what share expects it to fall. It reflects what the crowd is doing, not what the market will do. The economic calendar: knowing when the market may move The Economic Calendar section lists scheduled events with filters for yesterday, today, tomorrow and the week. Each entry shows how long is left until the event, the country, the event name and a strength indicator of one to three triangles. The more triangles, the bigger the event’s expected impact on the market. A routine government bond auction carries one, while a major employment report typically carries three. Alt: economic calendar Binarium This matters because prices often move sharply around big announcements. A beginner may prefer to avoid opening a trade minutes before a three-triangle release, while a more experienced trader may watch exactly those moments. Either way, it is better to know an event is coming than to be surprised by it. Event times follow the time zone set in the terminal’s Settings, so you can match them to West Africa Time. 3. Trading Signals and the Trading Room: ideas to learn from The Trading Room is a separate section in the terminal’s left-hand menu, and it is where Binarium’s trading signals appear. Access starts with the Business account, which the platform assigns once your total deposits reach around ₦750,000. Business and Premium accounts can enter the Business room, while VIP accounts can enter both the Business and VIP rooms. Inside, a feed of trade cards shows what selected traders, including verified pros, are trading. Each card lists the asset, expiry time and strike price. You choose whose trades appear in the feed. For someone learning, the value is educational. Seeing which assets and expiry times experienced traders pick shows how they think about the market. Treat every card as a hypothesis to check: look at the chart, decide your own stake, and test the approach on a demo account first. No trader’s call is guaranteed, including a professional’s. Advantages for Nigerian traders: naira accounts, local payments and NFX mode Beyond the tools, several details make Binarium easier to use from Nigeria. Account currency. Nigerian users can open an account in naira or in US dollars. You choose the currency at registration, and it cannot be changed later. Minimum amounts. The minimum deposit is ₦5,000. The minimum trade is around ₦1,000. Minimums can vary by payment system, so check the Cashier. Payment methods. The Cashier for Nigeria includes bank transfer, Visa cards and the local wallets OPay and PalmPay. Crypto options include Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT and USDC, as well as Binance Pay and Bybit Pay. Methods can change, so check the Cashier after registering. NFX mode. Besides the standard mode, where each asset shows its own payout percentage, Binarium offers NFX mode, where the payout is calculated for every trade separately. It depends on factors such as the number of active traders and the volatility of the asset. A variable payout does not change the risk: a wrong prediction still costs the full stake. Fees and withdrawals. Binarium states that it covers payment-system fees on deposits and withdrawals, subject to its terms. Identity verification is required before you withdraw. Getting started: promo code VANGUARD Binarium combines a demo account, TradingView charts, an economic calendar and a Trading Room with practical details for Nigerian users, from naira accounts to local payment methods. item.title: France reports first human Shamonda virus case, says no health risk
item.description: French health authorities said Thursday that the Shamonda virus, which usually affects livestock, had been detected in a human for the first time, in a severely immunocompromised patient who died earlier this month. There was “no health risk to the general public identified at this time”, the health and agriculture ministries said in a joint statement. It added that the human infection appeared to be “an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient” hospitalised for a serious medical condition. “Despite circulating in Africa and Asia for several decades, the Shamonda virus has never previously been detected in humans,” the ministries said. The virus, which belongs to the Orthobunyavirus group and is typically transmitted to animals by small biting insects, was first detected in Europe this summer, they said. At this stage in the investigation, the patient was believed to have contracted the virus through the bite of a midge in eastern France, where the virus was circulating in animals during the spring and summer, the ministries said. “The neurological complications observed in the immunocompromised patient prior to his death are very likely linked to infection with the Shamonda virus,” they added, citing preliminary findings. But “clinical, biological and epidemiological investigations are still ongoing”, they said. – In 14 European countries – The virus was first detected in Nigeria in the mid-1960s and has since been reported in cattle in several parts of Africa and in Japan. The virus was detected in Europe for the first time at the end of July, including on cattle farms in France. It has now been detected in 14 western European countries, according to an epidemiological bulletin from France’s national research institute monitoring animal health. Cattle are considered its main animal hosts, although sporadic infections in smaller livestock and horses have also been identified in France this summer. In cattle, the main symptoms are acute diarrhoea, fever, lethargy and a drop in milk production. An investigation is ongoing, and both the World Health Organization and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control have been notified. The post France reports first human Shamonda virus case, says no health risk appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Who won Lagos in 2023?
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Peter Obi of the Labour Party (LP) defeated Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Lagos State in the February 25, 2023, presidential election, overturning expectations in a state long regarded as Tinubu’s political stronghold. Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes, while Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) came third with 75,750 votes, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) received 8,442 votes. Obi won Lagos by 9,848 votes, making the result one of the major surprises of the 2023 presidential election. Tinubu, who governed Lagos from 1999 to 2007, had maintained significant political influence in the state through his party and political network. However, the result showed that his longstanding connection to Lagos did not guarantee victory at the polls. How Obi won Lagos According to the results published by INEC and reported by The Punch, Obi won nine of the state’s 20 local government areas, while Tinubu secured victories in the remaining 11. The Labour Party candidate performed strongly in Alimosho, Ojo, Oshodi-Isolo, Amuwo-Odofin, Eti-Osa, Ikeja, Kosofe, Somolu and Ajeromi-Ifelodun. In Alimosho, the state’s most populous local government area, Obi polled 71,327 votes against Tinubu’s 62,283. In Amuwo-Odofin, Obi recorded 55,547 votes, while Tinubu received 13,318. Obi also won Oshodi-Isolo with 51,020 votes against the APC candidate’s 27,181. Tinubu, meanwhile, won in areas including Agege, Apapa, Badagry, Epe, Ibeju-Lekki, Ifako-Ijaiye, Ikorodu, Lagos Island, Lagos Mainland, Mushin and Surulere. Despite winning more local government areas, Tinubu lost the overall contest because Obi accumulated more votes across the state. The result demonstrated the Labour Party’s ability to attract substantial support beyond the traditional structures of the APC and PDP. The outcome also reflected the appeal of Obi’s campaign among voters seeking an alternative to Nigeria’s established political parties, particularly young people who were prominent in the wider movement for political change. Election-day controversies The election in Lagos was also marked by reports of violence, intimidation and disruptions at some polling units. The Nigeria Civil Society Situation Room, which monitored the 2023 general elections, raised concerns about the scale of election-related violence in the state. Its report stated that “the incidents of violence in Lagos State appeared to have surpassed its existing threshold.” The report documented an incident at Bishop Oluwole Memorial Primary School in Ward 005, Ifako-Ijaiye, where a disagreement involving INEC officials and party agents over a voided ballot paper led to a fight during vote counting.
