item.dc:creator: Akinbayo Wahab
item.content:encoded: Sekinat Osundiji Peter Obi of the Labour Party (LP) defeated Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Lagos State in the February 25, 2023, presidential election, overturning expectations in a state long regarded as Tinubu’s political stronghold. Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes, while Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) came third with 75,750 votes, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) received 8,442 votes. Obi won Lagos by 9,848 votes, making the result one of the major surprises of the 2023 presidential election. Tinubu, who governed Lagos from 1999 to 2007, had maintained significant political influence in the state through his party and political network. However, the result showed that his longstanding connection to Lagos did not guarantee victory at the polls. How Obi won Lagos According to the results published by INEC and reported by The Punch, Obi won nine of the state’s 20 local government areas, while Tinubu secured victories in the remaining 11. The Labour Party candidate performed strongly in Alimosho, Ojo, Oshodi-Isolo, Amuwo-Odofin, Eti-Osa, Ikeja, Kosofe, Somolu and Ajeromi-Ifelodun. In Alimosho, the state’s most populous local government area, Obi polled 71,327 votes against Tinubu’s 62,283. In Amuwo-Odofin, Obi recorded 55,547 votes, while Tinubu received 13,318. Obi also won Oshodi-Isolo with 51,020 votes against the APC candidate’s 27,181. Tinubu, meanwhile, won in areas including Agege, Apapa, Badagry, Epe, Ibeju-Lekki, Ifako-Ijaiye, Ikorodu, Lagos Island, Lagos Mainland, Mushin and Surulere. Despite winning more local government areas, Tinubu lost the overall contest because Obi accumulated more votes across the state. The result demonstrated the Labour Party’s ability to attract substantial support beyond the traditional structures of the APC and PDP. The outcome also reflected the appeal of Obi’s campaign among voters seeking an alternative to Nigeria’s established political parties, particularly young people who were prominent in the wider movement for political change. Election-day controversies The election in Lagos was also marked by reports of violence, intimidation and disruptions at some polling units. The Nigeria Civil Society Situation Room, which monitored the 2023 general elections, raised concerns about the scale of election-related violence in the state. Its report stated that “the incidents of violence in Lagos State appeared to have surpassed its existing threshold.” The report documented an incident at Bishop Oluwole Memorial Primary School in Ward 005, Ifako-Ijaiye, where a disagreement involving INEC officials and party agents over a voided ballot paper led to a fight during vote counting. In another incident, at Polling Unit 069 in Amuwo-Odofin, the Situation Room reported that thugs attacked voters, vandalised vehicles and prevented some people from voting. The report also documented attacks on journalists covering the election. An ARISE TV crew was attacked in the Elegushi area of Lagos, leaving a cameraman with facial injuries, while camera drones and other equipment were seized. Beyond violence at polling units, the 2023 elections attracted criticism over the electronic transmission of results. INEC’s election report addressed glitches affecting its Result Viewing Portal (IReV) during the presidential election. The commission maintained that the technical problems did not invalidate the election, although the delays fuelled public concerns about transparency and the credibility of the process. These controversies formed part of the wider debate over the conduct of the 2023 general elections, with election observers calling for improvements in electoral administration, transparency and security. A significant political upset Ultimately, Obi’s victory in Lagos demonstrated that Tinubu’s political influence in the state was not enough to secure a presidential election win. Although the APC candidate won more local government areas, the Labour Party candidate prevailed on the total number of votes cast. With 582,454 votes against Tinubu’s 572,606, Obi emerged as the winner in Lagos by a margin of 9,848 votes. Atiku finished a distant third with 75,750 votes. The result became one of the defining stories of the 2023 presidential election, illustrating how voters in a state central to Tinubu’s political history chose a different candidate. item.title: Cynthia Erivo’s Fashion Range Is Beyond Impeccable
item.description: @jasonbolden If there’s one thing Cynthia Erivo has mastered, it’s the art of keeping us guessing. Whether she’s embracing full-throttle red carpet glamour or experimenting with more directional silhouettes, the British actress rarely plays it safe. And judging by her latest appearances, she’s showing no signs of slowing down. For the Prima Facie premiere at the BFI London Film Festival, Cynthia delivered a welcome dose of sunshine in a custom canary-yellow Prada gown. The bias-cut satin skimmed her figure beautifully, falling into a sweeping train, while oversized black grosgrain bows at the shoulders added a graphic contrast to the otherwise minimalist silhouette. @jasonbolden And she’s just as convincing in something that’s more casual but still directional. Case in point: the tan leather Proenza Schouler Fall 2026 co-ord she wore in New York. With its structured double-breasted jacket, relaxed trousers and chunky platform shoes, the look could easily have felt overwhelming. Instead, Cynthia made a compelling case for exaggerated proportions, proving that a neutral palette doesn’t have to mean playing it safe. Her final appearance at New York Comic Con, where she joined the cast of Children of Blood and Bone in another Proenza Schouler Fall 2026 creation also designed by new Proenza Schouler Creative Director Rachel Scott (also of Diotima). This time, she opted for a navy printed dress featuring sculptural draping, an asymmetric silhouette and dramatic fringed detailing. The silver grommets along the hem introduced an unexpected industrial edge, while glittering blue heels and statement jewellery completed the look. item.title: French city of Lyon bans ‘all protests’ on Saturday
item.description: Officials have banned “all protests” in France’s third-biggest city of Lyon on Saturday, ahead of nationwide demonstrations that day following rallies last weekend that descended into widespread street violence. The prefecture for the Rhone region said on Thursday in a statement to media that, “given the events of October 17, the prefect has decided to ban by decree all protests in the city of Lyon this Saturday, October 24”. Lyon, like Paris and other French cities, suffered clashes and looting when masked youths took to city centre streets on the sidelines of mass rallies protesting high inflation. The mayor of Lyon, Gregory Doucet, has said that his city experienced hours of “chaos” during the riots, with between 150 and 200 shops looted and a tourist office torched. Police arrested some 200 people. The organisers of the rallies, the Yellow Vest movement and unions, have called for another round of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living on Saturday, and a general strike and demonstrations on November 5. French officials who found themselves unable to contain last weekend’s violence this week ordered three nights of curfews in parts of Paris, Lyon and some other cities to protect shopping districts. item.title: [VIDEO] Why Vaccines Aren’t Available For Latest Ebola Outbreak — Africa CDC
item.description: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has explained why the continent has yet to find a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola disease. Speaking during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, the Director General of the Africa CDC, Dr. Jean Kaseya, said some partners consider Ebola an African issue, adding that “if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccines would already be available”. He, however, said that the agency had initiated clinical trials of new vaccines, including a new Bundibugyo vaccine manufactured in Egypt. item.title: Global race to update computers as AI discovers most disruptive hack yet
item.description: Critical vulnerabilities were detected in a widely used computer language, prompting cybersecurity authorities to advise affected websites and apps go offline until a fix became available ROB ENGELAAR/EPA/Shutterstock Cybersecurity experts around the globe are racing to update systems and prevent the most disruptive AI -enabled hack yet discovered. A flaw uncovered in widely used code has made 70 per cent of websites worldwide vulnerable to data theft and defacement. Government websites in France, Denmark, Finland and the Netherlands were taken offline as a precaution when the news emerged. Read more Will physics be the next field to be turned upside down by AI? PHP is a computer language commonly used in websites, but executed on a server. It is used to power interactive websites, such as the content management system WordPress, which runs news sites and blogs, social networks like Facebook and key reference tools like Wikipedia . Advertisement The issue actually involves two flaws, both found by cloud security company Wiz. They relate to how PHP handles errors involving memory: in certain circumstances, data can be left behind after an error, which can then be accessed by a malicious actor. That data can include private information, but it can also allow an attacker to run malicious code. Every PHP version released in the past decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, but the PHP Foundation, which oversees development, has already issued an update to overcome this . The foundation didn’t respond to a request for interview, but said in a blog post that signs of the vulnerability emerged in 2024. Yet nothing was done. This is because there was no immediately obvious practical way for hackers to exploit it at the time, and because there was debate about which of several fixes was most appropriate. Free newsletter Sign up to The Daily Sign up to newsletter “We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources,” the PHP Foundation said. In 2024, the flaw was thought to be impractical to take advantage of, but Alan Woodward at the University of Surrey, UK, says AI has moved the goalposts of what is possible since then. “It’s actually very, very difficult to exploit it. It requires millisecond timing,” says Woodward. “The reason it was thought to be too complicated was it would have taken a team of people yonks to actually work out the right timings. But what AI does, it doesn’t go for tea breaks, it doesn’t go home at 6 o’clock: you can just set loads of them running and eventually they’ll come up with the right answer of how to exploit it.” Wiz said in a blog post announcing the discovery that there are probably further bugs along similar lines in the PHP code base, which developers will also need to identify and rectify. item.content:encoded: Critical vulnerabilities were detected in a widely used computer language, prompting cybersecurity authorities to advise affected websites and apps go offline until a fix became available ROB ENGELAAR/EPA/Shutterstock Cybersecurity experts around the globe are racing to update systems and prevent the most disruptive AI -enabled hack yet discovered. A flaw uncovered in widely used code has made 70 per cent of websites worldwide vulnerable to data theft and defacement. Government websites in France, Denmark, Finland and the Netherlands were taken offline as a precaution when the news emerged. Read more Will physics be the next field to be turned upside down by AI? PHP is a computer language commonly used in websites, but executed on a server. It is used to power interactive websites, such as the content management system WordPress, which runs news sites and blogs, social networks like Facebook and key reference tools like Wikipedia . Advertisement The issue actually involves two flaws, both found by cloud security company Wiz. They relate to how PHP handles errors involving memory: in certain circumstances, data can be left behind after an error, which can then be accessed by a malicious actor. That data can include private information, but it can also allow an attacker to run malicious code. Every PHP version released in the past decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, but the PHP Foundation, which oversees development, has already issued an update to overcome this . The foundation didn’t respond to a request for interview, but said in a blog post that signs of the vulnerability emerged in 2024. Yet nothing was done. This is because there was no immediately obvious practical way for hackers to exploit it at the time, and because there was debate about which of several fixes was most appropriate. Free newsletter Sign up to The Daily Sign up to newsletter “We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources,” the PHP Foundation said. In 2024, the flaw was thought to be impractical to take advantage of, but Alan Woodward at the University of Surrey, UK, says AI has moved the goalposts of what is possible since then. “It’s actually very, very difficult to exploit it. It requires millisecond timing,” says Woodward. “The reason it was thought to be too complicated was it would have taken a team of people yonks to actually work out the right timings. But what AI does, it doesn’t go for tea breaks, it doesn’t go home at 6 o’clock: you can just set loads of them running and eventually they’ll come up with the right answer of how to exploit it.” Wiz said in a blog post announcing the discovery that there are probably further bugs along similar lines in the PHP code base, which developers will also need to identify and rectify. Wiz didn’t respond to a request for comment. People are vibe coding copyrighted apps with AI – will tech firms sue? Every time a new technology hits the internet, there is a battle between the rights of users and major companies. To see how this will play out with AI, columnist Jacob Aron looks to examples from the past Independent cybersecurity expert Junade Ali told the Science Media Centre that two thirds of websites use PHP and may be vulnerable to this latest technique. “The key long-term risk with these new vulnerabilities is that organisations fail to implement protections and update software, particularly in legacy systems,” said Ali. “The security posture of websites using PHP has dramatically improved over the past decade, but this highlights that this is an ever-present problem – particularly when AI agents are capable of remorselessly pursuing the goal of finding new vulnerabilities.” Woodward thinks that while most large websites will have already patched their systems, smaller sites with less expertise and resources could still be vulnerable months or years from now. “There will be this long tail and you’ll find some surprising sites have not been patched,” he says. AI has grown extremely capable in the field of cybersecurity over recent months, which includes working out how to hack computers and how to defend them from hackers, creating a destabilising effect that is yet to reach an equilibrium. 1000 human mathematicians pledge to shun AI in their research There is a growing backlash against the way AI companies have gone about tackling mathematical problems – and now some mathematicians are opting to avoid AI altogether In April, news broke of an unreleased AI model created by Anthropic called Mythos, which the company had kept under wraps because it had been found to be extremely good at hacking . The news sparked panic among cybersecurity experts. The National Health Service pulled its open-source projects , for instance, over fears Mythos may scour code for flaws and exploit its systems. Three months later, OpenAI admitted one of its prototype models had escaped a testing environment and hacked another company , Hugging Face. Not to be outdone, Anthropic announced within days that its Claude model had gone rogue and broken into machines at other companies on three occasions. We even learned from the National Cyber Security Centre, the UK government department tasked with securing the nation’s IT infrastructure, that the country’s four main cyber adversaries – Russia, China, North Korea and Iran – are using AI to boost their ability to perform “relentless” attacks on the UK .

item.title: Smirnoff Ice and BBNaija: A Season of Being Bolder with Ice
item.description: Three months, four pool parties, two Saturday night parties and one unforgettable task Smirnoff Ice has left its mark on the BBNaija house. The season was a full celebration of what Bolder with Ice stands for: self expression without limits. Inside the house, that meant housemates showing different sides of themselves depending on their mood, and the energy of the moment, and Smirnoff Ice was right there for every one of them. The pool parties set the tone early. With music playing and a cold Smirnoff Ice in hand, the housemates danced, had fun in the pool and laughed their way through every moment. Some stayed in the pool, others at the edge, while some didn’t stop dancing the whole time. That’s kind of the beauty of Bolder with Ice, there really isn’t a “ right ” way to experience it. You just show up, find your pace, and take it all in. Whether you’re there to lose yourself in the music or just relax with a cold drink, the whole point is simply being there and enjoying the moment. The Saturday night parties carried that same energy into the evening. The housemates stepped out in outfits they picked for themselves, danced to the music and enjoyed the night with their friends in the house. Every look and every dance move was theirs, which is exactly the kind of individuality the brand was built to celebrate. Then there was the Smirnoff Ice task: Bolder With Ice Challenge, where the house got to play, create and compete. Broken telephone, the Ice Throne styling challenge, the memory game, Shadow Partner and the painting round gave the housemates room to show their humour, their style, their focus and their creativity. Team Original and Team Double Black went head to head, but the real win was the laughter and the personality that came out of every round. That is what made the Smirnoff Ice season special. Across the pool parties, the Saturday night parties and the task, there was always room for every mood. The loud one, the quiet one, the stylish one, the playful one, the competitive one, all of them had a place and all of them had a good time. Smirnoff Ice did not ask the housemates to be anything other than themselves, and that is exactly the idea behind Bolder with Ice. As the season comes to an end, the memories will stay: the music, the pool, the dance floor, the games and the friendships built along the way. Thanks to every single housemate who brought their own kind of bold to the house, and a massive thank you to everyone who tuned in, laughed, and celebrated with us all season long. Until the next season, stay bold, stay chilled, and stay you. item.title: Anime's Most Devastating Horror Story Is a Tragedy About Being Human
item.description: But if you're looking for an anime that understands how horror can be both visually repulsive and emotionally devastating, Devilman Crybaby is the perfect series for you. Released on Netflix in 2018, Masaaki Yuasa's 10-episode adaptation of Go Nagai's Devilman is a spectacularly gruesome descent into the apocalypse. At its center is Akira Fudo, a sensitive young man forced into a horrific union with a demon to defend humankind from an existential threat. Granted immense power without sacrificing his empathy, Akira becomes a walking paradox: a creature born of unimaginable violence who still weeps for mankind. This core tension that propels the narrative, probing the fragile line between humanity and monstrosity.

item.title: NASA giving update about Artemis moon plans on Oct. 23: Watch it live
item.description: null NASA will provide an update about its Artemis moon plans on Friday (Oct. 23), and you can watch it live. The news will come during a press conference at the agency's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, which starts Friday at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA. "The update will include details about NASA’s Artemis III mission that will send four astronauts to low Earth orbit next year to test critical systems needed for future lunar landings, and how plans to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 are progressing," NASA officials said in an Oct. 14 media advisory . The crew of NASA's Artemis II mission captured this photo of a crescent Earth on April 6, 2026, as they began passing behind the moon. (Image credit: NASA) Three agency officials will participate in Friday's "Artemis Acceleration" event. They are: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager NASA is currently gearing up for Artemis III, which is targeted for mid-2027. The mission will test rendezvous and docking technologies between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the private spacecraft that NASA picked to be the Artemis program's crewed lunar landers: SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon . After that will come Artemis IV, which will land astronauts near the lunar south pole in early 2028, if all goes to plan. That will be the first crewed moon touchdown since Apollo 17 way back in 1972. It's unclear which lunar lander will fly on Artemis IV; that depends on how the development of each one progresses and what happens on Artemis III. And there will be other landings after Artemis IV. NASA plans to establish a moon base via Artemis, and doing so will require a variety of missions, both robotic and crewed. The agency feels some urgency in this quest, for China has similar goals . It's important that the U.S. wins this new space race, military and political officials have said , so that the nation can establish the norms of responsible behavior on Earth's nearest neighbor.
item.dc:creator: Mike Wall
item.content:encoded: null NASA will provide an update about its Artemis moon plans on Friday (Oct. 23), and you can watch it live. The news will come during a press conference at the agency's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, which starts Friday at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA. "The update will include details about NASA’s Artemis III mission that will send four astronauts to low Earth orbit next year to test critical systems needed for future lunar landings, and how plans to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 are progressing," NASA officials said in an Oct. 14 media advisory . The crew of NASA's Artemis II mission captured this photo of a crescent Earth on April 6, 2026, as they began passing behind the moon. (Image credit: NASA) Three agency officials will participate in Friday's "Artemis Acceleration" event. They are: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager NASA is currently gearing up for Artemis III, which is targeted for mid-2027. The mission will test rendezvous and docking technologies between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the private spacecraft that NASA picked to be the Artemis program's crewed lunar landers: SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon . After that will come Artemis IV, which will land astronauts near the lunar south pole in early 2028, if all goes to plan. That will be the first crewed moon touchdown since Apollo 17 way back in 1972. It's unclear which lunar lander will fly on Artemis IV; that depends on how the development of each one progresses and what happens on Artemis III. And there will be other landings after Artemis IV. NASA plans to establish a moon base via Artemis, and doing so will require a variety of missions, both robotic and crewed. The agency feels some urgency in this quest, for China has similar goals . It's important that the U.S. wins this new space race, military and political officials have said , so that the nation can establish the norms of responsible behavior on Earth's nearest neighbor.

item.title: IT department and auditors at major pharmacy chain got into a rip-roaring fight about using 'password' on Cisco firewall
item.description: Welcome back to PWNED, the column where we talk about companies and organizations that leave the doors wide open to attackers. This week’s sad story involves a major American pharmacy chain that couldn’t fill a prescription for password security. Have a story about someone leaving a gaping hole in their network? Share it with us at pwned@sitpub.com . Anonymity is available upon request. Our tale comes courtesy of red team and pen testing specialist Dahvid Schloss, who currently serves as COO of Suzu Labs , a cybersecurity company that boasts “we break your systems before adversaries do.” Over a career spanning more than 15 years, Schloss has assessed the security of numerous businesses, including a large US pharmacy retailer that he asked us not to name. He wasn’t asked to break in, just to do an audit on all of the org’s corporate switches, routers, and firewalls. “So, I come across this firewall,” Schloss said. “That is an edge firewall, meaning this is what touches the internet. This part will add its enable password, which is the term Cisco uses for administrator. It had the enable password as 'password.' Just p-a-s-s-w-o-r-d.” As Schloss noted, the enable command on Cisco devices allows the user to gain administrative rights to the firewall, controlling network traffic. If someone connected to that firewall, either via SSH or through an exploit, and got normal user privileges, they could then elevate those privileges to admin and do something like shut off all traffic from the intranet to the outside world. Schloss actually didn’t guess that the password was “password,” but instead was able to decrypt the file holding the passwords by breaking Cisco’s own protection, something he said is easy to do. “That enable password was stored as Cisco IOS type 7, which isn’t really a hash,” he said. “It’s more of a reversible encoding with a publicly known key. Even back then, it was best practice not to use it.” But even if the password were stored in a secure place, it would be very easy for a threat actor to guess. So he marked the password failure down as a “high find,” a bad type of vuln that needs to be fixed right away. When he brought the password to the company’s auditing department, they put him on a phone call with the auditing team, the entire IT team, his own manager, and others. On the packed call, the auditing team, who had commissioned Schloss’s work, was very concerned about the firewall password, but the IT team didn’t think it was a very serious problem. The two sides screamed at each other for more than an hour while Schloss and his colleagues sat there quietly, staring at their cameras. “The audit team is like ‘yeah, we gotta fix this.’ And the directors were really harping on ‘this needs to be done’ and the IT team starts firing back,” Schloss explained. “It’s like ‘Why? Who’s gonna? What does it matter? No, this isn’t a high-priority find. This is maybe a medium. Yeah, it’s bad, but it’s not that bad.’” The call dragged on so lon

item.content:encoded: Welcome back to PWNED, the column where we talk about companies and organizations that leave the doors wide open to attackers. This week’s sad story involves a major American pharmacy chain that couldn’t fill a prescription for password security. Have a story about someone leaving a gaping hole in their network? Share it with us at pwned@sitpub.com . Anonymity is available upon request. Our tale comes courtesy of red team and pen testing specialist Dahvid Schloss, who currently serves as COO of Suzu Labs , a cybersecurity company that boasts “we break your systems before adversaries do.” Over a career spanning more than 15 years, Schloss has assessed the security of numerous businesses, including a large US pharmacy retailer that he asked us not to name. He wasn’t asked to break in, just to do an audit on all of the org’s corporate switches, routers, and firewalls. “So, I come across this firewall,” Schloss said. “That is an edge firewall, meaning this is what touches the internet. This part will add its enable password, which is the term Cisco uses for administrator. It had the enable password as 'password.' Just p-a-s-s-w-o-r-d.” As Schloss noted, the enable command on Cisco devices allows the user to gain administrative rights to the firewall, controlling network traffic. If someone connected to that firewall, either via SSH or through an exploit, and got normal user privileges, they could then elevate those privileges to admin and do something like shut off all traffic from the intranet to the outside world. Schloss actually didn’t guess that the password was “password,” but instead was able to decrypt the file holding the passwords by breaking Cisco’s own protection, something he said is easy to do. “That enable password was stored as Cisco IOS type 7, which isn’t really a hash,” he said. “It’s more of a reversible encoding with a publicly known key. Even back then, it was best practice not to use it.” But even if the password were stored in a secure place, it would be very easy for a threat actor to guess. So he marked the password failure down as a “high find,” a bad type of vuln that needs to be fixed right away. When he brought the password to the company’s auditing department, they put him on a phone call with the auditing team, the entire IT team, his own manager, and others. On the packed call, the auditing team, who had commissioned Schloss’s work, was very concerned about the firewall password, but the IT team didn’t think it was a very serious problem. The two sides screamed at each other for more than an hour while Schloss and his colleagues sat there quietly, staring at their cameras. “The audit team is like ‘yeah, we gotta fix this.’ And the directors were really harping on ‘this needs to be done’ and the IT team starts firing back,” Schloss explained. “It’s like ‘Why? Who’s gonna? What does it matter? No, this isn’t a high-priority find. This is maybe a medium. Yeah, it’s bad, but it’s not that bad.’” The call dragged on so long that Schloss was unable to finish presenting his findings and recommendations. The conflict was so severe that the client continued to follow up and ask him to explain what he found again for the next three years – long after he had moved on to other projects. He later learned that the auditing department controlled the bonuses for the IT team and there was a stipulation that any “high finding” would eliminate those bonuses. So they weren’t just arguing about “password” - they were really talking about the compensation for an entire division. The lesson here is more than “don’t use the word ‘password’ as a password.” It's also about misaligned incentives. Tying security posture to compensation seems like a good way to incentivize workers to follow best practices, but it also leads them to deny responsibility and minimize mistakes when they're found. ®

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Will Get a Physical Release, But There's a Catch
item.description: With an increasing number of video game publishers moving away from physical releases, fans were worried that this would be the case with Phantom Blade Zero . Well, there's good news and bad news. The good news is that Phantom Blade Zero will, in fact, get a physical release. However, it will only be available a few months after launch.

item.title: Court Resumes Trial Of Suspects Linked To Abduction Of NYSC Members, Others In Imo
item.description: Court is set to resume the trial of suspects linked to the abduction of 20 members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and others in Imo State. The suspects were apprehended in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Abia State during intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 by the Department of State Services (DSS), in collaboration with the military, police, and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for the fleeing members of the gang. The prospective corps members were abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, while they were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The gunmen attacked two buses conveying the prospective corps members and other passengers near Umunoha in the Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State. The victims were rescued on October 7 during a joint security operation at Amakohia-Ubi Village in Owerri West Local Government Area of the state. They were subsequently taken to the DSS hospital in Owerri for medical attention and necessary checks. During the search-and-rescue operation, the police had said their operatives located the kidnappers’ camp through drone surveillance but could not immediately advance because the location was reportedly planted with improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Security agencies later intensified efforts to reach the victims and secure their release. The post Court Resumes Trial Of Suspects Linked To Abduction Of NYSC Members, Others In Imo appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Ebola: Medical laboratory scientists urge virtual campaigns ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: The Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists of Nigeria (AMLSN), Kaduna State Branch, has advised political parties to campaign virtually to minimise physical contact amid the Ebola outbreak. Mr Turman Benjamin, Chairman of the association in Kaduna gave the advice on Thursday in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Kaduna. Benjamin recommended social media, text messages, telephone calls and virtual meeting platforms such as Zoom and Google Meet as alternatives to physical political rallies. He said the approach would reduce unnecessary contact and help minimise potential exposure while health authorities worked to contain the outbreak. Benjamin urged the Kaduna State Government to intensify public awareness, trace any contacts linked to the confirmed case and ensure adequate protective equipment for healthcare workers. He advised residents to avoid unnecessary physical contact, including handshakes and hugs, and observe appropriate hygiene measures. The medical laboratory scientist said Ebola could be transmitted through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of infected persons. He also urged the public to avoid handling the bodies of suspected or confirmed Ebola victims without appropriate training and protective equipment. Benjamin said only trained and properly equipped personnel should handle such bodies to reduce the risk of infection during burial preparations. He called on the government to provide hospitals with adequate personal protective equipment, including gloves and other appropriate protective gear. According to him, laboratory testing is essential to confirm Ebola because its early symptoms can resemble those of other illnesses, including malaria and typhoid fever. Benjamin further advised the public to exercise caution when handling or consuming wild animals that could carry infectious diseases. He urged the media to intensify public education on Ebola transmission, prevention and the importance of seeking prompt medical attention when symptoms develop. The chairman also called for vigilance among healthcare workers and members of the public, stressing the importance of early detection and effective infection prevention measures. The NAN reports that the Federal Government has confirmed one case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, with 44 close contacts identified for monitoring to prevent further transmission. The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. The woman has since been placed in isolation and is receiving medical care, while health authorities have commenced contact tracing to identify and monitor people who may have been exposed to the virus.( NAN ) The post Ebola: Medical laboratory scientists urge virtual campaigns ahead of 2027 elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria – WHO
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the World Health Organization (WHO) saying there is no vaccine or specific treatment for the index Ebola virus case detected in Nigeria, which carried the Bundibugyo strain. Another headline features the Senate Committee on Public Accounts rejecting the volume of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) imports reported by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) for 2022 and 2023 over significant discrepancies with figures supplied by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL). Vanguard also reports that the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, said only 108 out of about 39,000 underage candidates who sat the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) have survived the Federal Government’s rigorous screening for possible admission into tertiary institutions. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian’s lead headline states that weak oversight and fiscal plan have left over 6,000 projects abandoned across the country, with their combined value running into trillions of naira. The Punch reports that the diplomat diagnosed with the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, has reportedly deteriorated into multi-organ failure, as the Federal Government and state governments intensify surveillance, contact tracing and emergency preparedness to prevent the spread of the deadly disease. Lastly, The Nation reports that Vice President Kashim Shettima challenged state governments to stop depending on the Federal Government for solutions to their electricity challenges. Vanguard News The post Nigerian newspapers review: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria – WHO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Troops rescue four kidnapped victims in Zamfara, Kebbi
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Sector 2, Operation Fansan Yamma, have rescued four kidnapped victims during separate intelligence-led operations in Zamfara and Kebbi states as the military intensifies efforts to combat terrorism and kidnapping across the North West. According to the Army, the victims were rescued on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, in Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State and between Bena and Sawade in Kebbi State. “In Zamfara, troops rescued Mansur Shehu, 25, and Kadijat Haruna, 49, following a response to a reported terrorist incident on farmland across a river in Binoni Marafa, Maru LGA. “In Kebbi, troops conducted a search-and-rescue operation after receiving reports of suspected terrorists moving with kidnapped victims from Dupindu Village, Kanya District, Danko-Wasagu LGA. “The operation secured the freedom of Jimoh Su-Arege, 35, and Kalahe Danjuma, 41, who were subsequently handed over to the Seriki of Dipindu. “The military said troops have continued to intensify patrols and surveillance across affected communities to strengthen security, dominate operational areas and deny criminal elements freedom of action. “The successful operations highlight Operation Fansan Yamma’s sustained efforts to rescue abducted persons, disrupt terrorist activities and restore peace across Zamfara and Kebbi states,” the military said. The post Troops rescue four kidnapped victims in Zamfara, Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Meta's Zuckerberg pitches AI successes to investors with 26% rise in quarterly revenue

item.title: UK government hasn't the foggiest how much it's spending on digital transformation
item.description: The UK government says its finance systems cannot produce consistent annual figures showing how much departments and public bodies spend on digital transformation. The Science and Technology Committee's June report warned that spending was fragmented and the government lacked a clear plan for a digital state. The UK public sector spends more than £26 billion annually on digital technology, but that broad estimate does not provide a comparable departmental breakdown. Responding to the committee, the government agreed with the "intent to publish annual data on digital and data-driven spending" but said it did not "believe this is currently practicable." Existing finance systems could not "provide consistent, reliable and comparable data across departments." "The government is open to this as a direction of travel and will work with HM Treasury to consider how this could be developed over time," the response said. Committee chair Dame Chi Onwurah, who is due to address Parliament on Thirsday, said: "There's no shortage of hype about how technology can improve public services and reduce costs. Yet, frustratingly, the government cannot provide a clear picture of how much is being spent on digital transformation across departments and public bodies. "At a time when ministers are asking taxpayers to fund significant investment in technology, it's concerning that they cannot show where the money is going or how value for money is being measured. This must be addressed as a matter of urgency." The government abolished the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology in the summer, dividing its responsibilities between the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport, the Cabinet Office, and the newly created Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade. Onwurah said: "Additionally, the abolition of DSIT has only highlighted concerns about who is responsible for driving digital transformation across government. I call on the government to revisit its response and create clear leadership that can drive and deliver the scale of change needed." The committee also called for the government to end Palantir's involvement in the NHS Federated Data Platform (FDP), citing concerns over sovereignty and vendor lock-in. The relationship has drawn criticism over £60 million in earlier contracts awarded without competition. The government said it would review the FDP contract "in line with standard contract management processes to inform a decision on whether to exercise the optional two-year extension." The response did not commit to an early exit. It said any termination would have to comply with the contract's terms and public procurement law. item.content:encoded: The UK government says its finance systems cannot produce consistent annual figures showing how much departments and public bodies spend on digital transformation. The Science and Technology Committee's June report warned that spending was fragmented and the government lacked a clear plan for a digital state. The UK public sector spends more than £26 billion annually on digital technology, but that broad estimate does not provide a comparable departmental breakdown. Responding to the committee, the government agreed with the "intent to publish annual data on digital and data-driven spending" but said it did not "believe this is currently practicable." Existing finance systems could not "provide consistent, reliable and comparable data across departments." "The government is open to this as a direction of travel and will work with HM Treasury to consider how this could be developed over time," the response said. Committee chair Dame Chi Onwurah, who is due to address Parliament on Thirsday, said: "There's no shortage of hype about how technology can improve public services and reduce costs. Yet, frustratingly, the government cannot provide a clear picture of how much is being spent on digital transformation across departments and public bodies. "At a time when ministers are asking taxpayers to fund significant investment in technology, it's concerning that they cannot show where the money is going or how value for money is being measured. This must be addressed as a matter of urgency." The government abolished the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology in the summer, dividing its responsibilities between the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport, the Cabinet Office, and the newly created Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade. Onwurah said: "Additionally, the abolition of DSIT has only highlighted concerns about who is responsible for driving digital transformation across government. I call on the government to revisit its response and create clear leadership that can drive and deliver the scale of change needed." The committee also called for the government to end Palantir's involvement in the NHS Federated Data Platform (FDP), citing concerns over sovereignty and vendor lock-in. The relationship has drawn criticism over £60 million in earlier contracts awarded without competition. The government said it would review the FDP contract "in line with standard contract management processes to inform a decision on whether to exercise the optional two-year extension." The response did not commit to an early exit. It said any termination would have to comply with the contract's terms and public procurement law. "If a decision is taken to not extend Palantir's contract, then the contract includes controls to support transition and continuity of services, ensuring that operational delivery and patient services are protected," the response said. Onwurah said the committee was pleased the government had committed to developing a strategy to tackle vendor lock-in and build greater internal capacity. "Ministers should now go further by exercising the break clause in its FDP contract and take steps to reduce our dependence on a small number of large US tech firms," she added. Palantir maintains that its technology provides value for money and helps the NHS improve efficiency. ®

item.title: Harry Kane admits wait to learn if he has won Ballon d’Or is ‘very stressful’ for family
item.description: Bayern Munich and England striker is odds-on favourite ‘I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to’ Harry Kane would love to know now whether he has won the Ballon d’Or because the uncertainty and constant questions are driving his family to distraction. But the Bayern Munich and England striker accepts the suspense before the big reveal at the London Palladium on Monday night is part of the show. Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the prestigious individual honour after a prolific run of form. The 33-year-old scored 61 goals for Bayern last season and 12 for England. This time out, he has 10 for Bayern and six for England. He scored from the penalty spot in Wednesday night’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena, although his stand-out moment was the inch-perfect through ball that set up Alphonso Davies to make it 1-1. Continue reading...

item.title: 'Popular dissatisfaction' across Europe: 'Promises of more economic growth haven't come true'
item.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Steven Erlanger, Chief Diplomatic Correspondent in Europe for The New York Times, based in Berlin. Europe's political centre is confronting a crisis that extends far beyond electoral volatility. From France and Germany to Italy and Spain, mounting economic frustration, generational inequality and declining confidence in established political leadership are reshaping the continent's democratic landscape. "The promises of more economic growth haven't come true," explains Erlanger, describing a continent marked by "a kind of general disgust" and "a sense of drift."

item.title: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort review – Wii Sports lives on in this effortlessly appealing collection of games
item.description: Nintendo Switch 2; Nintendo/Nintendo Bringing a holiday vibe and a generous selection of sport-themed games, this is exactly what you want from a family video game When the first Nintendo Switch Sports brought the effortless fun of Wii Sports back into my living room in 2022, I was frankly delighted . My small children discovered the pleasure of waving a controller around in enthusiastic imitation of a tennis player, and the surprising subtlety of virtual bowling, working out how to twist the wrist just right to guarantee a strike. I did not expect this game to become a family fixture for the next several years as my kids got older and climbed up the online ranks in all six of its sports (plus the two that were added as free updates). Switch Sports is so beloved in my household that the release of Switch Sports Resort this week is the most anticipated gaming event of the year. To be fair, my children are a bit young for Grand Theft Auto. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort brings three of the six sports back – tennis, bowling, and volleyball – alongside golf and basketball. Then there are seven entirely new sports: boxing, table tennis, archery, thumb wrestling, skateboarding, jetski, and piloting a little prop plane. They are all intuitive, easy to get the hang of on the first or second attempt – some have more legs than others, in the long run – and all of them, crucially, are a little bit silly. Thumb wrestling in particular is cheerfully absurd, giving your characters gigantic thumbs on hands the size of their heads. Continue reading...

item.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Planting an Okra Tree Taught Me About Life and Kindness
item.description: Dayo Akinbode narrates what planting an okra tree taught her about kindness. Credit: Dayo Akinbode Sometimes, the most beautiful things in our lives begin with a seed we never intended to plant. A s I stood in my garden admiring the green okro pods ready for harvest, I smiled. As I looked at the beautiful green pods, my thoughts travelled back several months to a seemingly insignificant encounter with my neighbour, which is the story behind my okra harvest. Earlier in the year, my neighbour offered me okro seeds to plant, but I declined them. I was not interested in planting okro, and I simply did not see the need. My neighbour, however, went ahead and planted the seeds in my garden. Imagine! So the seeds I declined were now nestled in the soil of my own garden, beginning a journey I had not planned for them. Those tiny seeds would eventually become flourishing plants that would supply my kitchen with fresh okro for months. I certainly did not imagine that I would one day stand admiring my harvest and reflecting on the deeper meaning of what had happened. Life has a way of surprising us like that. As the weeks passed, the plants grew, and I began to appreciate the beauty of watching nature at work. What begins as a tiny, almost insignificant seed gradually transforms into a living plant, reaching towards the light and preparing to produce something useful. And boy, there is something fascinating about harvesting food from your own garden. Whenever the flowers on the okra plants came – the yellow, hibiscus-like flowers – I knew harvest time was around the corner. Those bright splashes of yellow against the green leaves became a familiar and welcome sight. Each time I saw them, I felt a little excitement, knowing that fresh okro pods would soon appear, and then be ready for harvest. The bright yellow, hibiscus-like flowers of the okro plant, signalling that harvest time is approaching. Credit: Dayo Akinbode The process of planting okra is not so different to our l ives, too. We plant seeds when we start a business, pursue a dream, learn a new skill, nurture a friendship or encourage someone who is struggling. Sometimes, we see results quickly. At other times, progress appears slow, and we begin to wonder whether anything is happening at all. The absence of an immediate harvest does not necessarily mean that nothing is happening. Sometimes, growth is taking place quietly, beyond what we can see. And occasionally, there are little signs along the way that remind us to keep going, just as those yellow flowers reminded me that my okro harvest was approaching. As I reflected on this, I found myself thinking again about my neighbour and her simple act of kindness. She offered me something useful, and when I declined, she still found a way to share her gift with me. I wonder whether she imagined how much I would appreciate those plants months later. item.content:encoded: Dayo Akinbode narrates what planting an okra tree taught her about kindness. Credit: Dayo Akinbode Sometimes, the most beautiful things in our lives begin with a seed we never intended to plant. A s I stood in my garden admiring the green okro pods ready for harvest, I smiled. As I looked at the beautiful green pods, my thoughts travelled back several months to a seemingly insignificant encounter with my neighbour, which is the story behind my okra harvest. Earlier in the year, my neighbour offered me okro seeds to plant, but I declined them. I was not interested in planting okro, and I simply did not see the need. My neighbour, however, went ahead and planted the seeds in my garden. Imagine! So the seeds I declined were now nestled in the soil of my own garden, beginning a journey I had not planned for them. Those tiny seeds would eventually become flourishing plants that would supply my kitchen with fresh okro for months. I certainly did not imagine that I would one day stand admiring my harvest and reflecting on the deeper meaning of what had happened. Life has a way of surprising us like that. As the weeks passed, the plants grew, and I began to appreciate the beauty of watching nature at work. What begins as a tiny, almost insignificant seed gradually transforms into a living plant, reaching towards the light and preparing to produce something useful. And boy, there is something fascinating about harvesting food from your own garden. Whenever the flowers on the okra plants came – the yellow, hibiscus-like flowers – I knew harvest time was around the corner. Those bright splashes of yellow against the green leaves became a familiar and welcome sight. Each time I saw them, I felt a little excitement, knowing that fresh okro pods would soon appear, and then be ready for harvest. The bright yellow, hibiscus-like flowers of the okro plant, signalling that harvest time is approaching. Credit: Dayo Akinbode The process of planting okra is not so different to our l ives, too. We plant seeds when we start a business, pursue a dream, learn a new skill, nurture a friendship or encourage someone who is struggling. Sometimes, we see results quickly. At other times, progress appears slow, and we begin to wonder whether anything is happening at all. The absence of an immediate harvest does not necessarily mean that nothing is happening. Sometimes, growth is taking place quietly, beyond what we can see. And occasionally, there are little signs along the way that remind us to keep going, just as those yellow flowers reminded me that my okro harvest was approaching. As I reflected on this, I found myself thinking again about my neighbour and her simple act of kindness. She offered me something useful, and when I declined, she still found a way to share her gift with me. I wonder whether she imagined how much I would appreciate those plants months later. Whatever her motivation, her act taught me to be kind to people even when they can’t see or appreciate the value. We have all been there, one way or the other. This also made me wonder how many opportunities we dismiss because we cannot immediately see their value. A friend shares an idea we are not ready to embrace. Someone offers help we think we do not need. A person introduces us to an opportunity that seems unimportant at the time. We wave such opportunities away and move on, unaware of what might have grown from them. Of course, not every offer should be accepted, and we must exercise our judgement. We can learn to remain open to possibilities. Perhaps we can then enjoy the benefits of a decision we did not make ourselves, just as I am with the okra. Today, I am grateful for my okro harvest, and for my neighbour and her kindness. I am equally grateful for the reminder the okro growth has given me. Kindness can grow, patience can yield rewards, and an unexpected beginning can become a beautiful harvest. So, as I admire the fruits of my neighbour’s simple gesture, I find myself asking two questions: What seeds are we planting in the lives of others? And what beautiful harvest are we enjoying today because someone once planted a seed for us? item.title: Ogun shuts schools as over 100 pupils are hospitalised after gas emissions
item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Ogun State government has ordered the closure of some schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo following the hospitalisation of more than 100 pupils on Wednesday after suspected exposure to an offensive gaseous substance. The affected pupils were rushed to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode; the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo; and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools worst affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, Itamerin Comprehensive High School and some schools in Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed pupils reportedly fainting and being rushed to hospitals following the incident. The state government had previously identified the substance as methane, although the precise source of the recurring emissions remains under investigation. A teacher at one of the affected schools, who spoke to our correspondent on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 10am when pupils and staff began experiencing breathing difficulties, with some collapsing. “The pupils and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and were rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said. According to the teacher, some schools in Ago-Iwoye were forced to close at about 11am as the situation worsened. “The worst-hit schools include Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School and Anglican Girls Grammar School in Ijebu-Ode. Some parents who heard about the incident also came to pick up their children because nobody knew what was happening,” the teacher added. The teacher expressed concern over the recurring emissions, which have reportedly affected schools in the area since April, warning that pupils and staff continued to face potential health risks. “We are all anxious about our health and that of our pupils. I think it is taking the government too long to get to the root of this mysterious gas leakage. The government has to do something quickly before it gets too late,” the teacher said. Wednesday’s incident was the fourth reported occurrence of gaseous emissions in the Ijebu area since April, raising fresh concerns about the safety of pupils, teachers and other residents. In April, about 40 pupils were reportedly affected by the emissions, while more than 120 others were hospitalised following another incident in May. A further occurrence on June 1 reportedly left 69 pupils requiring medical attention. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Ogun State government has ordered the closure of some schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo following the hospitalisation of more than 100 pupils on Wednesday after suspected exposure to an offensive gaseous substance. The affected pupils were rushed to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode; the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo; and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools worst affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, Itamerin Comprehensive High School and some schools in Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed pupils reportedly fainting and being rushed to hospitals following the incident. The state government had previously identified the substance as methane, although the precise source of the recurring emissions remains under investigation. A teacher at one of the affected schools, who spoke to our correspondent on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 10am when pupils and staff began experiencing breathing difficulties, with some collapsing. “The pupils and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and were rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said. According to the teacher, some schools in Ago-Iwoye were forced to close at about 11am as the situation worsened. “The worst-hit schools include Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School and Anglican Girls Grammar School in Ijebu-Ode. Some parents who heard about the incident also came to pick up their children because nobody knew what was happening,” the teacher added. The teacher expressed concern over the recurring emissions, which have reportedly affected schools in the area since April, warning that pupils and staff continued to face potential health risks. “We are all anxious about our health and that of our pupils. I think it is taking the government too long to get to the root of this mysterious gas leakage. The government has to do something quickly before it gets too late,” the teacher said. Wednesday’s incident was the fourth reported occurrence of gaseous emissions in the Ijebu area since April, raising fresh concerns about the safety of pupils, teachers and other residents. In April, about 40 pupils were reportedly affected by the emissions, while more than 120 others were hospitalised following another incident in May. A further occurrence on June 1 reportedly left 69 pupils requiring medical attention. Schools previously affected included Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School, Epe Garage, Ijebu-Ode; Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode; and St Anthony Grammar School, Ijebu-Imusin, among others. The latest incident has renewed calls for the state government to establish the precise source of the emissions and implement a lasting solution to prevent further exposure. Following an earlier occurrence, Governor Dapo Abiodun said the state government was collaborating with the Ministries of Environment and Health, the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, and the Department of Geology at Olabisi Onabanjo University to determine the cause of the emissions. Abiodun disclosed that gas analysers had been installed in affected schools after the initial incident, while preliminary findings pointed to methane as the substance involved. “Preliminary findings suggest there may be geological factors involved, possibly fault lines common to these locations, which could be responsible for the emissions. “We are awaiting the final report from the professionals handling the investigation,” the governor said in June. When contacted on Wednesday, the state Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said the government was on top of the situation. Also speaking, the governor’s Senior Special Assistant and General Manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency, Kehinde Bello, who visited affected areas in Ijebu-Ode and Ijebu-Igbo, linked the latest incident to underground gas emissions previously recorded in the area. Bello said the situation was under control, assuring residents that the government would work towards finding a lasting solution to the recurring problem. He said the government’s investigations had indicated that the phenomenon was a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. Bello urged residents to remain calm, adding that the affected pupils were expected to recover after receiving medical attention. He also advised residents exposed to the odour to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks. As of the time of filing this report, medical personnel were attending to affected pupils at various hospitals. The recurring incidents have heightened concerns over the potential health risks posed by the emissions, particularly to schoolchildren and teachers, with residents awaiting the outcome of investigations and the implementation of measures to prevent further occurrences. item.title: NEMA Distributes Relief Materials To Gas Seepage-Affected Persons In Rivers Community
item.description: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) has distributed relief materials to persons affected by gas seepage in Bille Community, Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State. The intervention, carried out through NEMA’s Port Harcourt Operations Office, is aimed at easing the immediate humanitarian needs of residents affected by the incident. The exercise began with a courtesy visit to the King of Bille Kingdom, His Royal Majesty, King Igbikingeri Ngowari Cornelius. The delegation, representing the NEMA Director-General, Hajiya Umar, was led by Chidi Ogundu, who conveyed the agency’s message of sympathy to the monarch and the people of Bille Kingdom. The delegation later proceeded to Bille Community, where the relief materials were presented to community executives and leaders for distribution to affected persons. The exercise was conducted with measures in place to ensure an orderly and effective delivery of the assistance. Representatives of the Rivers State Emergency Management Agency (RISEMA) and the Nigerian Red Cross Society, alongside other stakeholders, witnessed the distribution. Community leaders expressed appreciation to NEMA and its Director-General for the intervention, saying the relief materials would help ease the hardship faced by residents. They also called for medical outreaches to help identify and address potential health problems associated with prolonged exposure to gas. The gas seepage, which began more than three months ago, is yet to receive a concrete solution from the Federal Government. Investigations into the incident are reportedly ongoing, involving the Federal Ministry of Gas, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), partners and operators. Residents continue to await a lasting solution to the problem and measures to address the potential health risks posed by prolonged exposure to the gas. The post NEMA Distributes Relief Materials To Gas Seepage-Affected Persons In Rivers Community appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: [UPDATED] Ebola Patient In Nigeria Is Ugandan-Born, Arrived Abuja October 3 — Africa CDC
item.description: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has disclosed that the index patient diagnosed with the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus in Nigeria is Ugandan-born and arrived in the Federal Capital Territory with her husband on October 3, 2026. ﻿ The Director General of the Africa CDC, Dr. Jean Kaseya, who stated this on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, said that though the regional agency was in talks with Nigeria, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo on ways to contain the outbreak, there was a need for the patient in Nigeria to provide relevant information to the authorities to avoid a crisis between African countries. “I am talking to all authorities — with Nigerian authorities, with Ugandan authorities, even to DRC authorities. But we are lucky that this person we know today, without any doubt, is a Ugandan-born person who went to Uganda and she was there for some days. Then the husband flew to join her in Uganda then they came back to Abuja on October 3. This is a fact,” said Kaseya. “Now, what we want is collaboration from this person, the lady. She has to disclose to the authorities. I need this information as Nigeria needs this information because we need also to support Uganda. She needs to tell us if, first, she flew to the DRC. Second, if she went out of Kampala; third, if she was in contact with someone who came from the DRC. “I think this is the information we are looking for. It will help all of us to avoid crisis between African countries.” ‘We’re Not In Panic Mode’ The Africa CDC DG, however, noted that the continent is now “well prepared” to address any public health issue. While pushing back on claims that Ebola is an African problem, he said that it would be a mistake to assume that anyone in the world is safe. A health worker stands in a new Ebola treatment centre during a visit of Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO), in Bunia, on May 31, 2026. (Photo by AFP) Kaseya, who disclosed that the Bundibugyo strain of the virus is the most geographically widespread, affecting West, Southern and East Africa, assured that the continent is not in a panic mode, as it knows what must be done. No Vaccine Yet For Bundibugyo Strain The Africa CDC DG said some partners consider Ebola an African issue, as “if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccines would already be available”. He, however, said that the agency had initiated clinical trials of new vaccines, including a new Bundibugyo vaccine manufactured in Egypt. A health official works in the laboratory extraction room of the Institute of Lassa Fever Research and Control in Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital in Irrua, Edo State, midwest Nigeria, on March 6, 2018. Photo by PIUS UTOMI EKPEI / AFP Kaseya also noted that the agency had worked with the DRC and Uganda to bring the Zaire vaccine for clinical trials and compassionate use. “We don’t want to see Africa left behind again. While pushing back on claims that Ebola is an African problem, he said that it would be a mistake to assume that anyone in the world is safe. A health worker stands in a new Ebola treatment centre during a visit of Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO), in Bunia, on May 31, 2026. (Photo by AFP) Kaseya, who disclosed that the Bundibugyo strain of the virus is the most geographically widespread, affecting West, Southern and East Africa, assured that the continent is not in a panic mode, as it knows what must be done. No Vaccine Yet For Bundibugyo Strain The Africa CDC DG said some partners consider Ebola an African issue, as “if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccines would already be available”. He, however, said that the agency had initiated clinical trials of new vaccines, including a new Bundibugyo vaccine manufactured in Egypt. A health official works in the laboratory extraction room of the Institute of Lassa Fever Research and Control in Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital in Irrua, Edo State, midwest Nigeria, on March 6, 2018. Photo by PIUS UTOMI EKPEI / AFP Kaseya also noted that the agency had worked with the DRC and Uganda to bring the Zaire vaccine for clinical trials and compassionate use. “We don’t want to see Africa left behind again. We have the knowledge. We have people with intelligence,” he said. “We have capacity to manufacture vaccines; we need to move on. This is also the case for medicine and diagnostics.” The Federal Government on Tuesday confirmed a case of the Ebola virus in the Federal Capital Territory, saying that the patient’s symptoms progressed four days after she arrived from Uganda, though the Ugandan authorities said there was no outbreak of the disease in the East African country . Pate is Nigeria’s health minister Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, told journalists in Abuja that while the patient had been placed in isolation and was receiving medical care, contact tracing had commenced, with 44 contacts already identified. Pate also said that surveillance had been strengthened at Nigeria’s entry points. The National Assembly urged the Federal Government to take urgent steps to contain the spread of the virus. The Senate on Wednesday called for the provision of emergency funding from the service-wide vote to strengthen the country’s disease surveillance system and enforce mandatory health screening at all international airports, seaports and designated land borders to prevent the spread of Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases. Similarly, the House of Representatives called for increased public awareness as well as early preparation of isolation camps following confirmation of a fresh outbreak in the FCT. Already, the Federal Government, through the Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development, has directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to place 46 people identified as contacts of an Ebola-affected patient on a no-fly list for at least 21 days. The post [UPDATED] Ebola Patient In Nigeria Is Ugandan-Born, Arrived Abuja October 3 — Africa CDC appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Iran’s Guards threaten to hit US bases in retaliation for Hormuz escorts
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. “The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website. “This is a serious warning,” they added. Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out in February. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation. But the US military has been escorting vessels through the waterway in increasing numbers, with Iran responding by stepping up attacks. Four ships were hit in the area overnight as they attempted to pass through the wider Gulf, Iranian forces said on Thursday. Washington has also been maintaining a naval blockade on Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the country’s economy, while negotiations to end the conflict are deadlocked. Hormuz, bordered to the north by Iran and to the south by Oman, is only about 30 kilometres (19 miles) wide at its narrowest point and is a critical route for ships carrying oil and gas from energy-rich Gulf countries. The post Iran’s Guards threaten to hit US bases in retaliation for Hormuz escorts appeared first on Vanguard News .
